/**
 * The focus-outline system — the InstUI focus ring, intrinsic to `base.css` so every focusable gets it
 * out of the box when pantoken owns the page. The resting element carries a transparent ring + a
 * transition, and `:focus-visible` reveals the colour and grows the offset. All rules are
 * zero-specificity `:where()`, so any component style overrides without `!important`.
 *
 * This is the one documented `@declaration` record, but it can't use `defineDeclaration` (its CSS is a
 * token block on one selector plus ring rules on another). Instead it exposes {@link focusOutlineCss}
 * (the bespoke builder `base.css` calls directly) and a {@link Definition}-shaped {@link focus} object
 * so the registry + `validate()` can treat it uniformly.
 *
 * @module
 */
import { focusOutlineDeclarations, focusOutlineRules } from "@pantoken/utils";
import { css } from "../lib/css.ts";
import type { Definition } from "../lib/define.ts";

// The pure focus-ring builders (`--instui-focus-outline-*` defs, the `:where()` ring rules, the
// focusable selector) now live in `@pantoken/utils`, so the token sheet (`@pantoken/css`) can emit the
// `:root` defs without depending on this package. Re-exported here so the `@pantoken/components` public
// surface is unchanged. This file keeps the cssdoc doc block, the header-wrapped `focusOutlineCss`, and
// the registry `Definition`.
export { FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR, focusOutlineDeclarations, focusOutlineRules } from "@pantoken/utils";

// prettier-ignore

 * @declaration focus
 * @class :focus-visible
 * @summary The focus-outline system: the \`--instui-focus-outline-*\` custom properties (declared on \`:root\`) plus the \`:focus-visible\` ring every focusable gets, and opt-in tuning classes.
 * @modifier -focus-color-success — Success-coloured ring.
 * @modifier -focus-color-danger — Danger-coloured ring.
 * @modifier -focus-color-inverse — Inverse (on-dark) ring.
 * @modifier -focus-position-inset — Draw the ring inset, inside the element's edge.
 * @modifier -focus-within — Ring the element while a descendant is focused.
 * @modifier -without-focus-animation — Disable the ring's grow-in animation.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color — The ring colour once focus is visible (the themed info colour).
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-start — The resting, transparent ring colour the outline transitions from.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-width — The outline width of the ring.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-offset — The gap between the element's edge and the ring when focused.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-radius — The ring's corner radius when focused.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-style — The outline line style (solid).
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-transition — The transition that animates the ring's colour and offset in.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-success — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-success\` modifier.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-danger — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-danger\` modifier.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-inverse — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-inverse\` (on-dark) modifier.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-inset — The outline offset used when \`-focus-position-inset\` draws the ring inside the edge.
 * @a11y Every focusable element gets a \`:focus-visible\` outline ring so keyboard users can see what's focused.
 * @example
 * <button class="instui-button -focus-color-danger">Delete</button>
 * @demo self:focus-outline
 */`;

/** The elements the ring applies to by default (the common interactive/focusable elements). */
export const FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR = "a, button, input, select, textarea, summary, [tabindex]";

const focusShared = (name: string): string =>
  `var(--instui-component-shared-tokens-focus-outline-${name})`;

/**
 * The `--instui-focus-outline-*` name/value pairs the ring rules read. Colour/width/offset reference
 * the themed shared focus tokens; the transition, line style, and inset are constants.
 *
 * @returns One `[customProperty, value]` pair per focus-ring variable.
 */
export function focusOutlineDeclarations(): [name: string, value: string][] {
  return [
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color", focusShared("info-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-start", "transparent"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-width", focusShared("width")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-offset", focusShared("offset")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-radius", "var(--instui-border-radius-md)"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-style", "solid"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-transition", "outline-color 0.2s, outline-offset 0.25s"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-success", focusShared("success-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-danger", focusShared("danger-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-inverse", focusShared("on-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-inset", "0rem"],
  ];

 * The focus-ring rules for a given focusable selector: a transparent resting ring that transitions in
 * on `:focus-visible`, plus the `-focus-color-*` / `-focus-position-inset` / `-focus-within` /
 * `-without-focus-animation` modifiers. All `:where()`-wrapped, so zero-specificity.
 *
 * @param selector - The focusable selector the base ring applies to (default {@link FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR}).
 * @returns The CSS rules string.
 */
export function focusOutlineRules(selector: string = FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR): string {
  return [
    `:where(${selector}) {`,
    `  outline: var(--instui-focus-outline-width) var(--instui-focus-outline-style) var(--instui-focus-outline-color-start);`,
    `  outline-offset: 0;`,
    `  transition: var(--instui-focus-outline-transition);`,
    `}`,
    `:where(${selector}):where(:focus-visible) {`,
    `  outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color);`,
    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,
    `  border-radius: var(--instui-focus-outline-radius);`,
    `}`,
    `:where(.-focus-color-success):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-success); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-color-danger):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-danger); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-color-inverse):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-inverse); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-position-inset):where(:focus-visible) { outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-inset); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-within):where(:focus-within) {`,
    `  outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color);`,
    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,
    `  border-radius: var(--instui-focus-outline-radius);`,
    `}`,
    `:where(.-without-focus-animation) { transition: none; }`,
  ].join("\n");
}

/**
 * Build the focus-outline block: the `--instui-focus-outline-*` token defs plus the ring rules.
 * Baked into `base.css` (so focusables get the ring out of the box), and reusable by other layered
 * outputs (e.g. the Pendo renderer) via the `selector`/`tokenSelector` options.
 *
 * @param options - `selector` — the focusable selector; `tokenSelector` — where the token defs land
 *   (default `:where(:root)`).
 * @returns The CSS string.
 *
 * @demo self:focus-outline
 */
export function focusOutlineCss(
  options: { selector?: string; tokenSelector?: string } = {},
): string {
  const tokenSelector = options.tokenSelector ?? ":where(:root)";
  const decls = focusOutlineDeclarations()
    .map(([name, value]) => `  ${name}: ${value};`)
    .join("\n");
  // prettier-ignore
  return css`${FOCUS_DOC}\n${tokenSelector} {\n${decls}\n}\n\n${focusOutlineRules(options.selector)}\n`;
}

/**
 * The {@link Definition}-shaped view of the focus declaration, so it can sit in the DECLARATIONS
 * registry and be checked by `validate()`. `css()`/`rules()` delegate to {@link focusOutlineCss} (its
 * default `instui`-prefixed output is a single well-formed declaration record).
 */
export const focus: Definition = {
  name: "focus",
  kind: "declaration",
  rules: () => focusOutlineCss(),
  css: () => focusOutlineCss(),
};

content.text:
I need to stop and bring you a material finding, because it invalidates the approved keystone.

## The lean-flatten premise was wrong

I built the `@property`-flatten lean mode and measured the real output. It barely helps:

| sheet | raw | **gzip** | brotli |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.css` (typed) | 1.58 MB | **141 KB** | 109 KB |
| `style.lean.css` (flattened) | 1.44 MB | **139 KB** | 107 KB |

Flattening `@property` → declarations saves **~2 KB gzip**, not the ~110 KB I'd projected. My earlier "~24 KB" estimate was a measurement bug — the data-URI values contain `;`, and my regex truncated them, so the fake lean sheet looked tiny. The `@property` boilerplate is highly repetitive and gzip erases it either way.

## Where the weight actually is

**1,777 `--instui-icon-*` data-URI tokens = 1.31 MB of the 1.64 MB raw.** The token sheet embeds the *entire* icon set as CSS custom properties. Strip the icons and the foundation is **raw 324 KB → gzip ~23 KB** — the real ~6x win.

Components reference only **11 distinct icons** (`check`, `chevron-down/right/up`, `circle-alert/check/x`, `info`, `minus`, `triangle-alert`, `x`), consumed as inlineable `url(data:...)` masks (e.g. `mask: var(--instui-icon-x)`). The other ~1,766 belong to the opt-in `icons.css` glyph sheet.

## What still stands vs. what changes

Most of the work is unaffected and correct: moving the builders to `@pantoken/utils`, emitting elevation/focus into the token sheet, the components de-dupe, and the `appendContribution` bug fix. **Only the "how do we shrink the foundation" lever changes** — from "flatten `@property`" (drop it; ~2 KB, not worth the typed-property tradeoff) to "**exclude the full icon set**." That raises one real decision: components need those 11 icons, so where do they come from?

=== getting-started.md head ===
# Getting started

pantoken takes Instructure UI's design tokens and icons, resolves them once, and reshapes that one
model into packages for many platforms: plain stylesheets, SCSS and Less, React and Vue and Svelte,
Tailwind and Panda, native Swift and Kotlin, WordPress and Drupal, Figma, and more.

You install the smallest package that fits your task. Everything is also re-exported by the unified
`pantoken` package, so you can start there and narrow down later.

## The token model

Tokens are CSS custom properties named `--instui-<group>-<name>`, for example
`--instui-color-background-brand` or `--instui-spacing-space-md`. Three themes ship: `rebrand`
(the default, with `light-dark()` where light and dark differ), `canvas`, and `canvasHighContrast`.
Icons are `<image>` tokens (`--instui-icon-<name>`) derived from Lucide plus Instructure's custom
glyphs.

## Style a web app

Install the stylesheet and import it once. It defines every `--instui-*` property, so you reference
them straight from your own CSS.

```sh
npm i @pantoken/css
```

```ts
import "@pantoken/css/inject";
```

input.content:
# CDN & distribution

pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.

## The token foundation

Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
variants ship:

- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.

The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
just the foundation loaded.

## Pick your components

jsDelivr's combine endpoint pulls the token foundation plus only the component stylesheets you need, in a
single request. Check the components you want, and the builder writes the URL:

<CdnPicker />

Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (about
0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
already carries them.

### Load order and fonts

Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` points at
font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css">
```

### Everything at once

To pull the whole component library instead of cherry-picking, point at the barrel (about 141 KB gzipped)
alongside the token sheet:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css">
```

## Web components

`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.

### ES modules (recommended)

An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css">
<script type="module">import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";</script>
```

Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.

To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### A classic script tag

For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
```

It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
only when you can't use modules.

## Pinning versions

The URLs above float to the latest release. Pin a major (or exact) version for production — for example
`@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you. The picker pins the current published version for
you.

## What's not here

There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.

# CDN és terjesztés

A pantoken minden csomagot közzétesz az npm-en, így a tokeneket, komponenseket és web-komponenseket
közvetlenül egy CDN-ről is behúzhatod — build lépés és bundler nélkül. Ez az oldal a CSS combine URL-t
(interaktív építővel) és a web-komponens beillesztéseket mutatja be.

## A token alap

Minden pantoken komponens `--instui-*` egyedi tulajdonságokat olvas be egy token lapból az oldalon. Két
változat érhető el:

- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — az ajánlott CDN alap. Minden tokent tartalmaz a teljes ikonkészlet
  kivételével, így körülbelül 23 KB gzip-elve.
- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — a teljes lap, benne mind a ~1777 ikon glyph tokennel
  (`--instui-icon-*`). Körülbelül 140 KB gzip-elve. Ezt töltsd be, ha széles körben hivatkozol ikonokra a
  `var(--instui-icon-*)` segítségével.

Az elevation skála és a fókuszgyűrű változói mindkét lapban benne vannak, így az árnyékok és a
fókuszgyűrű már önmagában az alappal is működnek.

## Válaszd ki a komponenseket

A jsDelivr combine végpontja egyetlen kérésben húzza be a token alapot és csak a szükséges komponens
stíluslapokat. Jelöld be a kívánt komponenseket, és az építő megírja az URL-t:

<CdnPicker />

Minden komponensfájl kicsi — a legtöbb körülbelül 2 KB. Az ikonokat megjelenítő komponensek (`alert`,
`checkbox` és néhány másik) igénylik ezeket a glyph-eket, ezért az építő hozzáadja a
`@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` fájlt (körülbelül 0,5 KB gzip-elve — a komponenskészlet által
használt 11 ikon), amikor a karcsú lapot választod. A teljes lap már tartalmazza őket.

### Betöltési sorrend és betűtípusok

Először a token alapot töltsd be, majd az opcionális alap resetet, végül a komponensfájlokat. A fenti
combine URL már ilyen sorrendben rakja őket. A betűtípusok az egyetlen kivétel: a
`@pantoken/components/fonts.css` relatív útvonalon hivatkozik a betűfájlokra, így a combine nem tudja
átírni őket — töltsd be saját `<link>` elemként:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css">
```

### Minden egyszerre

Ha a teljes komponenskönyvtárat szeretnéd behúzni válogatás helyett, mutass a gyűjtőlapra (körülbelül
141 KB gzip-elve) a token lap mellett:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css">
```

## Web-komponensek

A `@pantoken/web-components` keretrendszer-független `<instui-*>` egyedi elemeket regisztrál. Saját
CSS-üket beágyazzák, de a tokeneket továbbra is az oldalon lévő lapból olvassák, ezért egy token alapot is
tölts be.

### ES modulok (ajánlott)

Egy ESM CDN feloldja helyetted a csomag függőségeit. Ez minden elemet regisztrál:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css">
<script type="module">import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";</script>
```

Használd a teljes token lapot (vagy a karcsú lapot a `component-icons.css`-szel), hogy az ikonokat
megjelenítő elemek, például az `<instui-alert>`, feloldják a glyph-jeiket.

Ha csak néhány elemet szeretnél regisztrálni — a beágyazott függőségeikkel együtt —, importáld a
`register` függvényt, és add meg az `only` opciót:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // A date-input és a calendar automatikusan bekerül.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### Klasszikus script tag

# CDN és terjesztés

A pantoken minden csomagot közzétesz az npm-en, így a tokeneket, komponenseket és web-komponenseket
közvetlenül egy CDN-ről is behúzhatod — build lépés és bundler nélkül. Ez az oldal a CSS combine URL-t
(interaktív építővel) és a web-komponens beillesztéseket mutatja be.

## A token alap

Minden pantoken komponens `--instui-*` egyedi tulajdonságokat olvas be egy token lapból az oldalon. Két
változat érhető el:

- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — az ajánlott CDN alap. Minden tokent tartalmaz a teljes ikonkészlet
  kivételével, így körülbelül 23 KB gzip-elve.
- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — a teljes lap, benne mind a ~1777 ikon glyph tokennel
  (`--instui-icon-*`). Körülbelül 140 KB gzip-elve. Ezt töltsd be, ha széles körben hivatkozol ikonokra a
  `var(--instui-icon-*)` segítségével.

Az elevation skála és a fókuszgyűrű változói mindkét lapban benne vannak, így az árnyékok és a
fókuszgyűrű már önmagában az alappal is működnek.

## Válaszd ki a komponenseket

A jsDelivr combine végpontja egyetlen kérésben húzza be a token alapot és csak a szükséges komponens
stíluslapokat. Jelöld be a kívánt komponenseket, és az építő megírja az URL-t:

<CdnPicker />

Minden komponensfájl kicsi — a legtöbb körülbelül 2 KB. Az ikonokat megjelenítő komponensek (`alert`,
`checkbox` és néhány másik) igénylik ezeket a glyph-eket, ezért az építő hozzáadja a
`@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` fájlt (körülbelül 0,5 KB gzip-elve — a komponenskészlet által
használt 11 ikon), amikor a karcsú lapot választod. A teljes lap már tartalmazza őket.

### Betöltési sorrend és betűtípusok

Először a token alapot töltsd be, majd az opcionális alap resetet, végül a komponensfájlokat. A fenti
combine URL már ilyen sorrendben rakja őket. A betűtípusok az egyetlen kivétel: a
`@pantoken/components/fonts.css` relatív útvonalon hivatkozik a betűfájlokra, így a combine nem tudja
átírni őket — töltsd be saját `<link>` elemként:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css">
```

### Minden egyszerre

Ha a teljes komponenskönyvtárat szeretnéd behúzni válogatás helyett, mutass a gyűjtőlapra (körülbelül
141 KB gzip-elve) a token lap mellett:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css">
```

A `@pantoken/web-components` keretrendszer-független `<instui-*>` egyedi elemeket regisztrál. Saját
CSS-üket beágyazzák, de a tokeneket továbbra is az oldalon lévő lapból olvassák, ezért egy token alapot is
tölts be.

### ES modulok (ajánlott)

Egy ESM CDN feloldja helyetted a csomag függőségeit. Ez minden elemet regisztrál:

```html

<script type="module">import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";</script>
```

megjelenítő elemek, például az `<instui-alert>`, feloldják a glyph-jeiket.

Ha csak néhány elemet szeretnél regisztrálni — a beágyazott függőségeikkel együtt —, importáld a

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";

  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
```

csak akkor nyúlj hozzá, ha nem tudsz modulokat használni.

# pantoken

Instructure design tokens and icons, reshaped for every platform.

pantoken resolves Instructure UI's design tokens and icons once, then turns that single model into
many small, publishable packages: plain stylesheets, SCSS and Less, React and Vue and Svelte,
Tailwind and Panda, native Swift and Kotlin, WordPress and Drupal, Figma, and more. You install the
smallest package that fits your task, or the unified `pantoken` package that re-exports them all.

[Learn more](https://pantoken.iywahl.com)

## Quick start

Style a web app with the token stylesheet:

```sh
npm i @pantoken/css
```

```ts
import "@pantoken/css/inject";
```

```css
.button {
  background: var(--instui-color-background-brand);
  padding: var(--instui-spacing-space-md);
}
```

Or generate token source for a native platform, with no runtime dependency:

```sh
npx pantoken generate swift --out ./ios/Tokens --icons arrow-left,check-mark
```

## The token model

Tokens are CSS custom properties named `--instui-<group>-<name>`, for example
`--instui-color-background-brand`. Three themes ship: `rebrand` (the default, with `light-dark()`
where light and dark differ), `canvas`, and `canvasHighContrast`. Icons are `<image>` tokens
(`--instui-icon-<name>`) derived from Lucide plus Instructure's custom glyphs.

## Packages

The monorepo is organized into buckets. A few highlights:

| Bucket       | Contains                             | Examples                                                                    |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/`  | The model, core transformer, and CLI | `@pantoken/model`, `@pantoken/core`, `@pantoken/tokens`, `@pantoken/cli`    |
| `formats/`   | Token file formats                   | `@pantoken/css`, `@pantoken/scss`, `@pantoken/dtcg`, `@pantoken/icon-font`  |
| `renderers/` | Framework and tool integrations      | `@pantoken/react`, `@pantoken/vue`, `@pantoken/mui`, `@pantoken/pendo`      |
| `bundlers/`  | Build-tool plugins and presets       | `@pantoken/vite`, `@pantoken/next`, `@pantoken/tailwind`, `@pantoken/panda` |
| `platforms/` | Native and site-generator targets    | `@pantoken/swift`, `@pantoken/wordpress`, `@pantoken/rust`                  |
| `design/`    | Design-tool payloads                 | `@pantoken/figma`, `@pantoken/swatches`                                     |
| `plugins/`   | Optional token and CSS transforms    | `@pantoken/plugin-stacking`, `@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons`                |
| `tools/`     | Private build tooling                | `@pantoken/aggregate`, `@pantoken/validate-generated`                       |

The docs site has the [full package map](https://pantoken.iywahl.com/guide/packages).

## Architecture

`@pantoken/model` holds the type contracts. `@pantoken/core` is the only package that reads the
upstream source; it resolves tokens and icons into the canonical IR. `@pantoken/tokens` vendors that
IR as static JSON at build time, which is the decoupling point: downstream packages read
`@pantoken/tokens`, never `@pantoken/core`, so `npm i pantoken` never reaches for the GitHub-only
upstream. Every other bucket consumes the IR.

## Documentation

The site is built with VitePress and TypeDoc and deploys to GitHub Pages:
[pantoken.iywahl.com](https://pantoken.iywahl.com).

```sh
pnpm run docs:dev      # local dev server with hot reload
pnpm run docs:build    # production build
pnpm run docs:preview  # serve the production build
```

## Development

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run generate            # build every package, regenerating all generated/ output
pnpm run validate:generated  # build, then validate the generated output
pnpm run ready               # build, check, test, validate, and lint — the full gate
pnpm run check:publish       # publint every publishable package
```

Generated files are never committed — a build reproduces them into each package's `generated/`
directory. See the [generated-output guide](https://pantoken.iywahl.com/guide/generated-output).

## License

MIT

1	# CDN és terjesztés
2	
3	A pantoken minden csomagot közzétesz az npm-en, így a tokeneket, komponenseket és web-komponenseket
4	közvetlenül egy CDN-ről is behúzhatod — build lépés és bundler nélkül. Ez az oldal a CSS combine URL-t
5	(interaktív építővel) és a web-komponens beillesztéseket mutatja be.
6	
7	## A token alap
8	
9	Minden pantoken komponens `--instui-*` egyedi tulajdonságokat olvas be egy token lapból az oldalon. Két
10	változat érhető el:
11	
12	- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — az ajánlott CDN alap. Minden tokent tartalmaz a teljes ikonkészlet
13	  kivételével, így körülbelül 23 KB gzip-elve.
14	- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — a teljes lap, benne mind a ~1777 ikon glyph tokennel
15	  (`--instui-icon-*`). Körülbelül 140 KB gzip-elve. Ezt töltsd be, ha széles körben hivatkozol ikonokra a
16	  `var(--instui-icon-*)` segítségével.
17	
18	Az elevation skála és a fókuszgyűrű változói mindkét lapban benne vannak, így az árnyékok és a
19	fókuszgyűrű már önmagában az alappal is működnek.
20	
21	## Válaszd ki a komponenseket
22	
23	A jsDelivr combine végpontja egyetlen kérésben húzza be a token alapot és csak a szükséges komponens
24	stíluslapokat. Jelöld be a kívánt komponenseket, és az építő megírja az URL-t:
25	
26	<CdnPicker />
27	
28	Minden komponensfájl kicsi — a legtöbb körülbelül 2 KB. Az ikonokat megjelenítő komponensek (`alert`,
29	`checkbox` és néhány másik) igénylik ezeket a glyph-eket, ezért az építő hozzáadja a
30	`@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` fájlt (körülbelül 0,5 KB gzip-elve — a komponenskészlet által
31	használt 11 ikon), amikor a karcsú lapot választod. A teljes lap már tartalmazza őket.
32	
33	### Betöltési sorrend és betűtípusok
34	
35	Először a token alapot töltsd be, majd az opcionális alap resetet, végül a komponensfájlokat. A fenti
36	combine URL már ilyen sorrendben rakja őket. A betűtípusok az egyetlen kivétel: a
37	`@pantoken/components/fonts.css` relatív útvonalon hivatkozik a betűfájlokra, így a combine nem tudja
38	átírni őket — töltsd be saját `<link>` elemként:
39	
40	```html
41	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
42	```
43	
44	### Minden egyszerre
45	
46	Ha a teljes komponenskönyvtárat szeretnéd behúzni válogatás helyett, mutass a gyűjtőlapra (körülbelül
47	141 KB gzip-elve) a token lap mellett:
48	
49	```html
50	<link
51	  rel="stylesheet"
52	  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
53	/>
54	```
55	
56	## Web-komponensek
57	
58	A `@pantoken/web-components` keretrendszer-független `<instui-*>` egyedi elemeket regisztrál. Saját
59	CSS-üket beágyazzák, de a tokeneket továbbra is az oldalon lévő lapból olvassák, ezért egy token alapot is
60	tölts be.
61	
62	### ES modulok (ajánlott)
63	
64	Egy ESM CDN feloldja helyetted a csomag függőségeit. Ez minden elemet regisztrál:
65	
66	```html
67	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
68	<script type="module">
69	  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
70	</script>
71	```
72	
73	Használd a teljes token lapot (vagy a karcsú lapot a `component-icons.css`-szel), hogy az ikonokat
74	megjelenítő elemek, például az `<instui-alert>`, feloldják a glyph-jeiket.
75	
76	Ha csak néhány elemet szeretnél regisztrálni — a beágyazott függőségeikkel együtt —, importáld a
77	`register` függvényt, és add meg az `only` opciót:
78	
79	```html
80	<script type="module">
81	  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
82	  // A date-input és a calendar automatikusan bekerül.
83	  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
84	</script>
85	```
86	
87	### Klasszikus script tag
88	
89	Modulok nélküli beillesztéshez töltsd be az IIFE buildet. Ez beágyazza a függőségeit, betöltéskor minden
90	elemet automatikusan regisztrál, és egy `PantokenWebComponents` globális objektumot tesz elérhetővé:
91	
92	```html
93	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
94	<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
95	```
96	
97	Nagyobb, mint az ESM út — beágyazza a `@pantoken/components` és a `@pantoken/icons` csomagokat —, ezért
98	csak akkor nyúlj hozzá, ha nem tudsz modulokat használni.
99	
100	## Verziók rögzítése
101	
102	A fenti URL-ek a legfrissebb kiadásra mutatnak. Éles környezetben rögzíts egy fő (vagy pontos) verziót —
103	például `@pantoken/css@0` —, hogy egy frissítés soha ne érjen váratlanul. Az építő helyetted rögzíti az
104	aktuálisan közzétett verziót.
105	
106	## Ami nincs itt
107	
108	Nincs `?components=button,badge` lekérdezési paraméter: egyetlen nyilvános CDN sem állít össze bundle-t
109	lekérdezési paraméterekből. A combine URL a legközelebbi megfelelő, és az építő megírja helyetted.

1	# CDN & distribution
2	
3	pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
4	from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
5	builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.
6	
7	## The token foundation
8	
9	Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
10	variants ship:
11	
12	- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
13	  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
14	- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
15	  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
16	  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.
17	
18	The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
19	just the foundation loaded.
20	
21	## Pick your components
22	
23	jsDelivr's combine endpoint pulls the token foundation plus only the component stylesheets you need, in a
24	single request. Check the components you want, and the builder writes the URL:
25	
26	<CdnPicker />
27	
28	Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
29	and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (about
30	0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
31	already carries them.
32	
33	### Load order and fonts
34	
35	Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
36	above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` points at
37	font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:
38	
39	```html
40	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
41	```
42	
43	### Everything at once
44	
45	To pull the whole component library instead of cherry-picking, point at the barrel (about 141 KB gzipped)
46	alongside the token sheet:
47	
48	```html
49	<link
50	  rel="stylesheet"
51	  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
52	/>
53	```
54	
55	## Web components
56	
57	`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
58	own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.
59	
60	### ES modules (recommended)
61	
62	An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:
63	
64	```html
65	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
66	<script type="module">
67	  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
68	</script>
69	```
70	
71	Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
72	`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.
73	
74	To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:
75	
76	```html
77	<script type="module">
78	  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
79	  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
80	  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
81	</script>
82	```
83	
84	### A classic script tag
85	
86	For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
87	element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:
88	
89	```html
90	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
91	<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
92	```
93	
94	It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
95	only when you can't use modules.
96	
97	## Pinning versions
98	
99	The URLs above float to the latest release. Pin a major (or exact) version for production — for example
100	`@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you. The picker pins the current published version for
101	you.
102	
103	## What's not here
104	
105	There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
106	The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.

Implementation complete and fully verified. Here's what landed.

## What shipped

**The keystone (Part 0 + A) — a lean token foundation.** Mid-implementation I measured the actual output and found the approved premise was wrong: flattening `@property` saved only ~2 KB gzip (the boilerplate compresses to nothing). The real weight is the **1,777 icon data-URI tokens**. You chose the fix — exclude the icon set. So:
- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — the full sheet minus `--instui-icon-*`: **294 KB raw → 22.5 KB gzip / 17.4 KB brotli** (~6× smaller), keeping `@property` typing intact (no visual-parity risk).
- Elevation + focus-outline builders moved down to `@pantoken/utils`; `@pantoken/css` emits them into **both** sheets via a foundation plugin. The `components.css` barrel and `base.css` no longer redefine them.
- `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` — the **11 icons** components actually use (549 bytes gzip), auto-detected at build. Picking an icon-using component adds it to the combine URL against the lean sheet.
- Fixed a real latent bug in `appendContribution` (plugin `@property` with a `var()` initial-value emitted invalid CSS).

**Web components (Part B).** `register(customElements, { only: [...] })` with automatic nested-dependency expansion (`date-time-input → date-input → calendar`), the foundation injection retired, and a new `dist/web-components.iife.js` `<script>` drop-in (`PantokenWebComponents` global).

**Docs (Part C).** An interactive `<CdnPicker />` (sourced from a generated manifest, i18n'd for `hu`) that live-builds the jsDelivr combine URL, plus a `CDN & distribution` guide (English + Hungarian) and a README pointer.

## Verification — all green
- `vp run ready:all` and `gate:publish` both pass (build, tests, lint, typecheck, exports).
- New unit tests pass: lean-sheet composition, the `appendContribution` guard fix, `register({ only })` + nested deps, the icon-completeness guard, and the foundation-moved-out assertions.
- **Browser-verified**: the picker builds correct pinned URLs and toggles work ([screenshot]); and a component renders standalone against **only** the lean foundation + `component-icons.css` — alerts show their icon glyphs and elevation shadows, proving the moved foundation and icon subset resolve with no barrel and no full icon set.

## Deviations from the approved plan (worth flagging)
1. **Keystone pivoted** from `@property`-flatten to icon-exclusion (measured, then you approved `component-icons.css`).
2. `@pantoken/utils` became a runtime dep of `@pantoken/components` too (not just `@pantoken/css`) — the published barrel imports the builders at runtime, so devDep wasn't correct.
3. The "animated custom-property guard" became an **icon-completeness guard**, since dropping flatten made the animation concern moot.
4. The IIFE is ~210 KB gzip (it inlines the token IR via `@pantoken/components`) — documented as a convenience target, not the recommended path.

The plan file still describes the original flatten approach; I left it as the historical record rather than rewriting it. Want me to update it to reflect the final icon-exclusion design?

# CDN & distribution for pantoken CSS and web components

> **Status: implemented and verified.** This file reflects what was actually built. The keystone changed
> during implementation — see "Keystone correction" below — from flattening `@property` to excluding the
> icon set, after measuring that flattening saved only ~2 KB gzip.

## Context

pantoken ships small, individually-publishable packages, but there was no CDN story for the
Bootstrap-style "drop in a URL" experience, and per-component modularization was undercut by the size of
the mandatory token foundation. Two asks:

1. **CSS** — pull an incremental subset of components through one URL (via `@import`/`<link>`), with an
   interactive docs picker — and make it pay off by shrinking the token foundation loaded alongside it.
2. **Web components** — same idea, plus a classic `<script src>` drop-in and true per-component
   cherry-picking.

## Keystone correction (measured during implementation)

The approved plan assumed the token sheet's bulk was `@property` typing boilerplate, so a
declaration-only "lean" sheet would drop it from ~137 KB to ~25 KB gzip. **That was wrong.** Measuring the
real output:

- Flattening `@property` → `:root` declarations saved only **~2 KB gzip** (141 → 139). The boilerplate is
  highly repetitive and gzip erases it either way. (The earlier ~24 KB estimate was a measurement bug: the
  data-URI values contain `;`, and the estimating regex truncated them.)
- **86% of the sheet (1.31 MB raw of 1.64 MB) is the 1,777 `--instui-icon-*` data-URI tokens.** Excluding
  the full icon set drops the foundation to **294 KB raw → 22.5 KB gzip / 17.4 KB brotli** — the real ~6×
  win, with `@property` typing kept intact (so no typed-property/visual-parity tradeoff).
- Components reference only **11 distinct icons** (`check`, `chevron-*`, `circle-*`, `info`, `minus`,
  `triangle-alert`, `x`), consumed as `url(data:…)` masks.

Decision taken (with the user): the lean sheet **omits the full icon set**; the ~11 component-referenced
icons ship separately as `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css`. The `@property`-flatten machinery was
dropped; only the `appendContribution` guard fix (below) was kept.

---

## Part 0 — Lean token sheet + icon split (keystone)

- **`formats/css/src/index.ts`** — `export const leanCss = toCss(tokens.filter(t => !t.name
  .startsWith("--instui-icon-")), { plugins: [foundationPlugin] })`, alongside the full `css`. Icon
  exclusion is a plain token filter — no `toCss` API change needed for it.
- **`formats/css/src/to-css.ts`** — kept the guard fix only: `appendContribution` now routes any
  plugin-contributed property whose initial-value is contextual (`var()`/`light-dark()`) to a `:root`
  declaration instead of emitting an invalid `@property`. (No `lean`/`keepTyped` options — those were part
  of the abandoned flatten approach.)
- **`formats/css/scripts/generate.ts`** — writes `generated/style.lean.css` next to `style.css`.
- **`formats/css/vite.config.ts`** — `style.lean` pack entry.
- **`formats/css/package.json`** — `"./style.lean.css"` export.
- **Tests** (`formats/css/tests/to-css.test.ts`): `leanCss` has no `--instui-icon-`, keeps
  elevation/focus, is < half the size, and is self-contained (no dangling refs); plus the guard-fix test.

## Part A — Move elevation + focus-outline into the token sheet

### A1. Relocate the pure builders to `@pantoken/utils`
`elevationDeclarations`, `focusOutlineDeclarations`, `focusOutlineRules`, `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, and the
elevation constants moved from `formats/components/src/declarations/{elevation,focus}.ts` into
`packages/utils/src/declarations.ts` (re-exported from the utils barrel). `@pantoken/utils` depends only
on `@pantoken/model` + arkregex — no cycle. **Promoted `@pantoken/utils` from devDep → runtime dep in
BOTH `formats/css/package.json` and `formats/components/package.json`** (deviation from the plan's "keep
components on devDep": the published `@pantoken/components` barrel's `componentsCss()` calls the builders
at runtime, so they're a genuine runtime dep). The builders are pure, Node-free string functions.

### A2. Emit them from `@pantoken/css`
A `definePlugin` foundation plugin appends elevation (8) + focus-outline (11) declarations. Values are
contextual, so they land as `:root` declarations in **both** `css` and `leanCss`.

### A3. De-dupe in `@pantoken/components` + emit `component-icons.css`
- `componentsCss()` no longer leads with `elevationCss()`; `baseCss()` emits `focusOutlineRules()` only
  (the ring rules stay; the vars now come from the token sheet). Both keep *referencing* the vars.
- The moved builders are re-exported from the components barrel + declaration files (so `elevationCss`/
  `focusOutlineCss`, the cssdoc `Definition`s, pendo, and `scripts/generate.ts` keep working unchanged).
- **`formats/components/scripts/generate.ts`** emits `generated/component-icons.css`: the `--instui-icon-*`
  glyph tokens the component sheets reference (auto-detected via `var(--instui-icon-…)`, valued from the
  token IR — throws if one is missing). Registered as an aggregate in `vite.config.ts` + a
  `"./component-icons.css"` export. Result: 11 icons, ~549 bytes gzip.

### A4. Retire the web-components foundation injection
`renderers/web-components/src/index.ts` — removed `foundationCss()` + the `<style id=pantoken-foundation>`
injection in `register()` (redundant now the required token sheet carries them); updated the module JSDoc
to note lean-sheet users pair with `component-icons.css`.

### A6. Tests
`formats/components/tests/{sheets,rules/base}.test.ts` updated: components.css no longer defines the
elevation `:root` block; base.css references but no longer defines `--instui-focus-outline-*`; the
IR-drift filter comment updated. Added an **icon-completeness guard** (replaces the plan's now-moot
"animated custom-property guard", since flatten was dropped): every `--instui-icon-*` a component
references must exist in the token IR, so `component-icons.css` fully backs the lean foundation.

**Combine URL (foundation = lean sheet):**
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css@0/style.lean.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/component-icons.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/alert.css">
```
`component-icons.css` is added only when a chosen component uses icons and the lean sheet is selected;
`base.css` is optional; `fonts.css` always a separate plain `<link>` (relative `url()`, not combine-safe).

## Part B — Web components

- **B1** — Documented the ESM CDN path (esm.sh / `+esm`), auto-registers all elements.
- **B2** — `renderers/web-components/scripts/build-iife.ts` (direct Vite `build()` call, no nested `vp`)
  emits `dist/web-components.iife.js`: IIFE, `PantokenWebComponents` global, deps inlined, auto-registers
  on load. Wired into the build task after `vp pack`. ~210 KB gzip (inlines the token IR via
  `@pantoken/components`) — a documented convenience target, not the default.
- **B3** — `register(target, { only })` filters `DEFINITIONS` (canonical order preserved) and expands a
  `NESTED_DEPS` map (`date-time-input → date-input → calendar`). Auto-`register()` (all) stays the
  default. Tests cover the subset + transitive expansion.

## Part C — Docs

- **`docs/scripts/cdn-manifest.ts`** (wired into `docs:assets`) emits
  `.vitepress/theme/generated/cdn-manifest.json` from the `COMPONENTS` registry: shippable component names
  (`kind: "component"`), per-component `needsIcons`, and the current `@pantoken/components`/`@pantoken/css`
  versions.
- **`docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue`** (+ `theme/cdn.ts` defaults) — registered globally
  in `enhanceApp`. Builds the combine URL live from checkboxes: lean/full token sheet, `<link>`/`@import`,
  optional base reset, auto-added `component-icons.css`, Copy button, pinned versions. Labels routed
  through `i18n.ts` → `themeConfig.cdnPicker` (English + Hungarian).
- **`docs/guide/cdn.md`** (+ `docs/hu/guide/cdn.md`) embedding `<CdnPicker />`; sidebar entry
  (`sidebar.cdn`) in `i18n.ts` + `config.ts`; README pointer.

## Verification (all passed)

1. `vp run ready:all` + `vp run gate:publish` — build, tests, lint, typecheck, export resolution: green.
2. Lean sheet: `dist/style.lean.css` = 294 KB raw / **22.5 KB gzip**, zero `--instui-icon-`, elevation +
   focus present. `component-icons.css` = 11 icons / 549 bytes gzip.
3. Standalone render (static server over the dist files): an `.instui-alert` renders with correct colors,
   **elevation box-shadow**, and its **icon glyph** against only `style.lean.css` + `component-icons.css`
   + `alert.css` — no barrel, no full icon set. (Screenshot captured.)
4. Per-component register: unit tests — `only` subset + `date-time-input` pulling in `date-input` +
   `calendar`, in canonical order.
5. IIFE built; valid IIFE, `PantokenWebComponents` global, no bare imports.
6. Docs picker (vitepress dev): builds correct pinned URLs; lean/full toggle adds/drops
   `component-icons.css`; `<link>`/`@import` switch; i18n renders.

## Deviations from the approved plan

- **Keystone**: icon-exclusion, not `@property`-flatten (measured; flatten ≈ 2 KB, icons ≈ 118 KB gzip).
- `@pantoken/utils` promoted to a runtime dep of `@pantoken/components` too (barrel imports it at runtime).
- Guard test is icon-completeness, not animation (flatten dropped → no animation risk).
- IIFE is ~210 KB gzip (bundles the token IR) — documented convenience target.

## Risks / notes

- jsDelivr combine mishandles relative `url()` — keep `fonts.css` out of combine (verified everything else
  is `data:`-URI only).
- The lean sheet drops the full `var(--instui-icon-*)` set; consumers using icons broadly load the full
  token sheet (or `icons.css`).
- No `?components=…` query-param builder — the combine URL is the closest off-the-shelf equivalent.

`elevationDeclarations`, `focusOutlineDeclarations`, `focusOutlineRules`, `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, and the
elevation constants moved from `formats/components/src/declarations/{elevation,focus}.ts` into
`packages/utils/src/declarations.ts` (re-exported from the utils barrel). `@pantoken/utils` depends only
on `@pantoken/model` + arkregex — no cycle. **Promoted `@pantoken/utils` from devDep → runtime dep in
BOTH `formats/css/package.json` and `formats/components/package.json`** (deviation from the plan's "keep
components on devDep": the published `@pantoken/components` barrel's `componentsCss()` calls the builders
at runtime, so they're a genuine runtime dep). The builders are pure, Node-free string functions.

### A2. Emit them from `@pantoken/css`
A `definePlugin` foundation plugin appends elevation (8) + focus-outline (11) declarations. Values are
contextual, so they land as `:root` declarations in **both** `css` and `leanCss`.

### A3. De-dupe in `@pantoken/components` + emit `component-icons.css`
- `componentsCss()` no longer leads with `elevationCss()`; `baseCss()` emits `focusOutlineRules()` only
  (the ring rules stay; the vars now come from the token sheet). Both keep *referencing* the vars.
- The moved builders are re-exported from the components barrel + declaration files (so `elevationCss`/
  `focusOutlineCss`, the cssdoc `Definition`s, pendo, and `scripts/generate.ts` keep working unchanged).
- **`formats/components/scripts/generate.ts`** emits `generated/component-icons.css`: the `--instui-icon-*`
  glyph tokens the component sheets reference (auto-detected via `var(--instui-icon-…)`, valued from the
  token IR — throws if one is missing). Registered as an aggregate in `vite.config.ts` + a
  `"./component-icons.css"` export. Result: 11 icons, ~549 bytes gzip.

### A4. Retire the web-components foundation injection
`renderers/web-components/src/index.ts` — removed `foundationCss()` + the `<style id=pantoken-foundation>`
injection in `register()` (redundant now the required token sheet carries them); updated the module JSDoc
to note lean-sheet users pair with `component-icons.css`.

### A6. Tests
`formats/components/tests/{sheets,rules/base}.test.ts` updated: components.css no longer defines the
elevation `:root` block; base.css references but no longer defines `--instui-focus-outline-*`; the
IR-drift filter comment updated. Added an **icon-completeness guard** (replaces the plan's now-moot
"animated custom-property guard", since flatten was dropped): every `--instui-icon-*` a component
references must exist in the token IR, so `component-icons.css` fully backs the lean foundation.

**Combine URL (foundation = lean sheet):**
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css@0/style.lean.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/component-icons.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/alert.css">
```
`component-icons.css` is added only when a chosen component uses icons and the lean sheet is selected;
`base.css` is optional; `fonts.css` always a separate plain `<link>` (relative `url()`, not combine-safe).

## Part B — Web components

- **B1** — Documented the ESM CDN path (esm.sh / `+esm`), auto-registers all elements.
- **B2** — `renderers/web-components/scripts/build-iife.ts` (direct Vite `build()` call, no nested `vp`)
  emits `dist/web-components.iife.js`: IIFE, `PantokenWebComponents` global, deps inlined, auto-registers
  on load. Wired into the build task after `vp pack`. ~210 KB gzip (inlines the token IR via
  `@pantoken/components`) — a documented convenience target, not the default.
- **B3** — `register(target, { only })` filters `DEFINITIONS` (canonical order preserved) and expands a
  `NESTED_DEPS` map (`date-time-input → date-input → calendar`). Auto-`register()` (all) stays the
  default. Tests cover the subset + transitive expansion.

## Part C — Docs

- **`docs/scripts/cdn-manifest.ts`** (wired into `docs:assets`) emits
  `.vitepress/theme/generated/cdn-manifest.json` from the `COMPONENTS` registry: shippable component names
  (`kind: "component"`), per-component `needsIcons`, and the current `@pantoken/components`/`@pantoken/css`
  versions.
- **`docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue`** (+ `theme/cdn.ts` defaults) — registered globally
  in `enhanceApp`. Builds the combine URL live from checkboxes: lean/full token sheet, `<link>`/`@import`,
  optional base reset, auto-added `component-icons.css`, Copy button, pinned versions. Labels routed
  through `i18n.ts` → `themeConfig.cdnPicker` (English + Hungarian).
- **`docs/guide/cdn.md`** (+ `docs/hu/guide/cdn.md`) embedding `<CdnPicker />`; sidebar entry
  (`sidebar.cdn`) in `i18n.ts` + `config.ts`; README pointer.

1. `vp run ready:all` + `vp run gate:publish` — build, tests, lint, typecheck, export resolution: green.
2. Lean sheet: `dist/style.lean.css` = 294 KB raw / **22.5 KB gzip**, zero `--instui-icon-`, elevation +
   focus present. `component-icons.css` = 11 icons / 549 bytes gzip.
3. Standalone render (static server over the dist files): an `.instui-alert` renders with correct colors,
   **elevation box-shadow**, and its **icon glyph** against only `style.lean.css` + `component-icons.css`
   + `alert.css` — no barrel, no full icon set. (Screenshot captured.)
4. Per-component register: unit tests — `only` subset + `date-time-input` pulling in `date-input` +
   `calendar`, in canonical order.
5. IIFE built; valid IIFE, `PantokenWebComponents` global, no bare imports.
6. Docs picker (vitepress dev): builds correct pinned URLs; lean/full toggle adds/drops
   `component-icons.css`; `<link>`/`@import` switch; i18n renders.

## Deviations from the approved plan

- **Keystone**: icon-exclusion, not `@property`-flatten (measured; flatten ≈ 2 KB, icons ≈ 118 KB gzip).
- `@pantoken/utils` promoted to a runtime dep of `@pantoken/components` too (barrel imports it at runtime).
- Guard test is icon-completeness, not animation (flatten dropped → no animation risk).
- IIFE is ~210 KB gzip (bundles the token IR) — documented convenience target.

content.thinking:
I need to set up a new branch and organize the changes into logical commits before pushing and opening a PR. Let me check the current git state and group these modifications—the utils builders migration with CSS updates and foundation emission, the component deduplication with icon styles, and the remaining changes in part A4.

Now I'm thinking through the commit ordering to ensure each one is coherent and respects dependencies. The utils builders move needs to happen first since the component deduplication and CSS emission depend on it, so I'll start with moving the elevation and focus builders to the utils package along with the lean token sheet and foundation emission. I'm running into a file-overlap problem where `css/package.json` needs changes in both commits—the utils dependency in commit 1 and the style.lean export in commit 2. Rather than split one file across commits, I should consolidate these changes into a single commit to keep things clean. I'm settling on a practical approach: put the utils declarations and components refactoring together in the first commit, then handle the CSS package changes and lean stylesheet export separately in the second commit, since pnpm-lock will capture both dependency promotions anyway. I'm running into a package.json conflict—the components package needs both the utils dependency and the component-icons.css export, but they're being touched across different commits. I could put components/package.json in commit 3 with both changes, but then commit 1's utils move wouldn't declare the dependency upfront, though it'd still resolve through the workspace. For cleaner commit coherence, the dependency should land alongside the move itself.

The cleanest approach is using `git add -p` to split the package.json changes interactively—the utils-dep hunk and the export hunk are in different parts of the file, so I can stage them separately across commits. This way commit 1 gets the utils move plus the dependency hunks, commit 2 gets the CSS export, and commit 3 gets the components export.

But `git add -p` is interactive and the Bash tool doesn't support that. I could use patches or scripts, but that's overcomplicating it. The user wants incremental, logical commits—not necessarily perfect file isolation. A pragmatic approach where each package.json appears once with all its changes is fine and still keeps the work organized by feature.

So I'll structure this as three commits: first moving the elevation and focus builders to utils, then updating the CSS format with the new foundation and icon-free token sheet, and finally updating components to use the token sheet and add the component icons export.

Then for web-components, I'm retiring the foundation injection approach and adding a register function with an optional `only` parameter, plus building an IIFE bundle for direct script inclusion. Finally, I'll add CDN documentation with an interactive picker component to help users choose the right distribution method. I'm realizing the lockfile needs to be grouped with whichever commit actually changes the dependencies. Since the utils promotion happens in commit 2 or 3 where package.json gets updated, the pnpm-lock.yaml should go there to keep everything coherent. Let me reorganize so the dependency changes and lockfile update are in the same commit. Commit 1 creates a dependency issue: utils gets moved and components starts importing from @pantoken/utils, but the dependency isn't declared in components/package.json until commit 3. This breaks buildability between commits 1 and 3 since the import won't resolve properly without the explicit dependency, even though the workspace symlink might technically make it work during development.

For a PR that's reviewed as a whole and merged, intermediate non-buildability is acceptable, but to be safe I should include the utils dependency promotion and lockfile updates in commit 1 itself so the move is complete and coherent. However, that means touching package.json files in both commit 1 (for the dependency) and commits 2/3 (for the export lines), which would require hunk-level staging across multiple commits. Since that's not cleanly doable, I'll accept that each package.json gets modified across commits as a pragmatic tradeoff. C1 includes the utils files and their re-exports from components, plus the CSS package updates and lockfile. The components package.json gets the utils dependency here since its declarations import from utils, though components will also need the icon export added later. formats/components/vite.config.ts, formats/components/package.json, formats/components/tests/generate.test.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml
- C4 refactor(css): consolidate elevation/focus into shared foundation module
    formats/css/src/foundation.ts, formats/css/src/index.ts, formats/css/tests/foundation.test.ts
- C5 refactor(components): update to use shared foundation
    formats/components/src/index.ts, formats/components/tests/generate.test.ts

So the breakdown is: C1 moves the builders to utils, C2 adds the lean CSS sheet and emits elevation/focus, C3 sources from that sheet and adds component icons, C4 consolidates the shared foundation, and C5 updates components to use it. Each file appears exactly once across the commits.

For the branch name, I'm thinking `feat/lean-token-sheet` or `feat/foundation-consolidation` since the core work is extracting and consolidating the foundation tokens.

Let me set up the commits now. I'll create the branch, stage each commit logically, and push with a PR. The commit messages will follow conventional style with bodies explaining the changes, and I'll add the Co-Authored-By trailer as specified.

## What & why

Enables Bootstrap-style CDN distribution for pantoken CSS and web components, and makes per-component modularization actually pay off by shrinking the mandatory token foundation.

The bottleneck was the token sheet: ~140 KB gzip, **86% of it the ~1,777 `--instui-icon-*` data-URIs**. A component doesn't need the whole icon set, so this ships a **lean, icon-free token sheet (~22.5 KB gzip)** as the CDN foundation, plus a tiny `component-icons.css` (the 11 icons components actually use). "Foundation + one button" is now roughly the size of all of Bootstrap's CSS.

> **Note:** the original plan flattened `@property` registrations for the size win. Measuring the real output showed that saved only ~2 KB gzip — the icons are the weight. The approach pivoted to icon-exclusion (keeping `@property` typing intact, so no visual-parity tradeoff).

**CSS**
- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — full sheet minus the icon set (~22.5 KB gzip / 17.4 KB brotli).
- Elevation + focus-outline composites moved down to `@pantoken/utils`, emitted into **both** sheets, so a component resolves shadows and its focus ring against the token sheet alone.
- `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` — the 11 component-referenced icons (~0.5 KB gzip), auto-detected at build.
- Fixed a latent `appendContribution` bug (plugin `@property` with a `var()` initial-value emitted invalid CSS).

**Web components**
- `register(customElements, { only: [...] })` with automatic nested-dependency expansion (`date-time-input → date-input → calendar`).
- New `dist/web-components.iife.js` `<script>` drop-in (`PantokenWebComponents` global); retired the now-redundant foundation injection.

**Docs**
- A `CDN & distribution` guide (English + Hungarian) with an interactive `<CdnPicker />` that live-builds the jsDelivr combine URL (component checkboxes, lean/full toggle, `<link>`/`@import`, pinned versions, auto icon sheet), sourced from a generated manifest and i18n'd.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css@0/style.lean.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/component-icons.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/alert.css">
```

- `vp run ready:all` and `vp run gate:publish` both green (build, tests, lint, typecheck, exports).
- New tests: lean-sheet composition, the `appendContribution` guard fix, `register({ only })` + nested deps, icon-completeness guard, foundation-moved-out assertions.

## Notes
- `@pantoken/utils` is now a runtime dep of `@pantoken/components` (the published barrel calls its builders at runtime).
- The IIFE is ~210 KB gzip (it inlines the token IR) — a documented convenience target, not the recommended path.

content.content:
name: Deploy docs

# Build the VitePress + TypeDoc site and publish it to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.
#
# Gated behind CI: this runs after the CI workflow finishes on main and only deploys when CI passed,
# reusing the packages CI already built (downloaded as an artifact) instead of rebuilding the
# workspace. `workflow_dispatch` is the manual escape hatch — it builds the assets fresh (for a
# `[skip ci]` commit, or to re-run a failed deploy), since the CI artifact won't exist for it.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # download the build-output artifact from the triggering CI run
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Deploy only after a successful CI run (or a manual dispatch), and — for a CI-triggered run — only
  # when the pushed commit actually changed something the site renders.
  changes:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      should_deploy: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.should_deploy }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Decide whether to deploy
        id: decide
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            exit 0
          fi
          # The site is themed by generated token/CSS output from many packages, so treat those as
          # deploy-worthy too (broad but correct). Compare the pushed commit to its parent.
          if git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | grep -qE '^(docs/|packages/|formats/|platforms/|renderers/web-components/|plugins/|design/|pnpm-lock\.yaml|pnpm-workspace\.yaml)'; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          else
            echo "should_deploy=false" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            echo "No docs-relevant changes in this push; skipping deploy."
          fi

  build:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.should_deploy == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

The drift check is separate from the build process itself; it validates that the committed cache covers all current English content.

The fix is straightforward: run the translation command locally to update the cache and Hungarian files, then commit the cache directory. This workflow requires both the Claude code adapter for guides and the glossary adapter for API content.

content.text:
Fixed. **[PR #14 — fix(docs): commit hu translation cache](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/14)** on `fix/docs-locale-cache`.

## What went wrong

The docs deploy failure wasn't the build — it was `check-locale-drift`. The site's Hungarian pages are machine-translated from a committed cache (`docs/i18n-cache/`), and that check fails if any current English block lacks a cache entry. The CDN work added new English prose (the `cdn.md` guide plus the API doc comments I changed — `leanCss`, `componentsCss`, `baseCss`, `register`, etc.) with no cache entries. CI generates translations but can't commit them, so the post-merge deploy on `main` failed in ~50s.

My hand-written `hu/guide/cdn.md` didn't help — the drift check wants the cache, not the file.

## The fix

Ran `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:locales:translate` (the claude-code adapter — `claude` was on PATH) to translate the 9 drifted blocks and refresh the cache + hu pages, then committed:
- `docs/i18n-cache/hu.{guides,api}.json` — new entries, stale keys pruned
- `docs/hu/guide/cdn.md` — regenerated by the pipeline (replaces my stopgap)
- `docs/hu/guide/packages.md` — table-padding re-normalization only, content identical

## Verified
- `check-locale-drift` ✓ and `check-locale-parity` ✓
- The exact deploy command `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build` completes clean in ~70s

Once #14 merges, the Deploy docs workflow will re-run on `main` and pass.

One minor note: TypeDoc emits a *warning* (not an error) for the `{@link NESTED_DEPS}` reference in the `register` doc comment (it's a private const). It doesn't fail the build. I left it as-is because editing that doc comment would change its English and re-trigger translation drift — not worth the churn for a warning.

## Direct answer

Yes — and it's four packages, not just two. jsDelivr serves published npm tarballs, and the merged CDN work never got a version-bumping changeset (the one on `main` was tooling-only with empty frontmatter). So `style.lean.css` and `component-icons.css` don't exist at `@pantoken/css@0.1.0` / `@pantoken/components@0.1.1`. The release must bump:

- **`@pantoken/utils`** (minor) — owns the moved elevation/focus builders that css + components import at runtime; must publish first so the others' `workspace:*` dep pins to a version that has them

- **`@pantoken/web-components`** (minor) — `register({ only })` + IIFE

`changeset status` confirms exactly those four bump minor; dependent renderers get the configured patch bump.

## How it lands

1. Merge **#15** → the changesets action opens a **"Version Packages"** PR.
2. Merge that PR → it bumps versions and **publishes to npm**.
3. The docs redeploy regenerates the picker manifest from the new `package.json` versions, so the combine URLs point at versions that actually contain the files.

## Ordering note

Until step 2 publishes, the picker's URLs stay broken (they pin `0.1.x`). And merge **#14** (the docs locale-cache fix) first or alongside — otherwise the docs deploy keeps failing on the drift check regardless of the release. So: **#14 → #15 → the Version Packages PR**, then the CDN URLs resolve.

<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from "vue";
import { useData } from "vitepress";
import { CDN_PICKER_DEFAULTS, type CdnPickerStrings } from "../cdn";
import manifest from "../generated/cdn-manifest.json";

type ManifestComponent = { name: string; needsIcons: boolean };
const { componentsVersion, cssVersion } = manifest as {
  componentsVersion: string;
  cssVersion: string;
  components: ManifestComponent[];
};
// Alphabetical for findability (the manifest is in load order).
const components = [...(manifest.components as ManifestComponent[])].sort((a, b) =>
  a.name.localeCompare(b.name),
);

// Localized labels from the active locale's themeConfig.cdnPicker, falling back to English defaults.
const { theme } = useData();
const t = computed<CdnPickerStrings>(() => ({
  ...CDN_PICKER_DEFAULTS,
  ...(theme.value as { cdnPicker?: Partial<CdnPickerStrings> }).cdnPicker,
}));

const selected = ref<Set<string>>(new Set());
const tokenSheet = ref<"lean" | "full">("lean");
const includeBase = ref(false);
const format = ref<"link" | "import">("link");
const copied = ref(false);

function toggle(name: string): void {
  const next = new Set(selected.value);
  if (next.has(name)) next.delete(name);
  else next.add(name);
  selected.value = next;
  copied.value = false;
}

const chosen = computed(() => components.filter((c) => selected.value.has(c.name)));
// The lean token sheet omits icons, so a selected icon-using component needs component-icons.css. The
// full sheet already carries every icon.
const needsIconSheet = computed(
  () => tokenSheet.value === "lean" && chosen.value.some((c) => c.needsIcons),
);

const combineUrl = computed(() => {
  const c = `npm/@pantoken/components@${componentsVersion}`;
  const files = [
    `npm/@pantoken/css@${cssVersion}/${tokenSheet.value === "lean" ? "style.lean.css" : "style.css"}`,
  ];
  if (includeBase.value) files.push(`${c}/base.css`);
  if (needsIconSheet.value) files.push(`${c}/component-icons.css`);
  for (const comp of chosen.value) files.push(`${c}/${comp.name}.css`);
  return `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/${files.join(",")}`;
});

const output = computed(() =>
  format.value === "link"
    ? `<link rel="stylesheet" href="${combineUrl.value}">`
    : `@import url("${combineUrl.value}");`,
);

async function copy(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(output.value);
    copied.value = true;
    setTimeout(() => (copied.value = false), 1500);
  } catch {
    // Clipboard blocked — the code stays selectable in the block.
  }
}
</script>

# CDN & distribution

pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.

## The token foundation

Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
variants ship:

- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.

The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
just the foundation loaded.

## Pick your components

jsDelivr's combine endpoint pulls the token foundation plus only the component stylesheets you need, in a
single request. Check the components you want, and the builder writes the URL:

<CdnPicker />

Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (about
0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
already carries them.

### Load order and fonts

Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` points at
font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
```

### Everything at once

To pull the whole component library instead of cherry-picking, point at the barrel (about 141 KB gzipped)
alongside the token sheet:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
/>
```

## Web components

`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.

### ES modules (recommended)

An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
<script type="module">
  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
</script>
```

Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.

To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### A classic script tag

For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
```

It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
only when you can't use modules.

## Pinning versions

The URLs above float to the latest release. Pin a major (or exact) version for production — for example
`@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you. The picker pins the current published version for
you.

## What's not here

There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.

own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.

### ES modules (recommended)

An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
<script type="module">
  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
</script>
```

Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.

To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### A classic script tag

For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
```

It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
only when you can't use modules.

## Pinning versions

The URLs above float to the latest release. Pin a major (or exact) version for production — for example
`@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you. The picker pins the current published version for
you.

## What's not here

There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.
