attachment.snippet:
1	# CDN és terjesztés
2	
3	A pantoken minden csomagot közzétesz az npm-en, így közvetlenül egy CDN-ből lekérheti a tokeneket, komponenseket és webes komponenseket – nincs szükség fordítási lépésre vagy csomagolóra. Ez az oldal a CSS kombinált URL-t (interaktív szerkesztővel) és a webes komponensek csatlakozásait ismerteti.
4	
5	## A token alapja
6	
7	Minden pantoken komponens `--instui-*` egyéni tulajdonságokat olvas az oldalon lévő tokenlapból. Két variáns érkezik:
8	
9	- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — az ajánlott CDN alapja. Minden tokent tartalmaz a teljes ikontárgykészlet kivételével, így körülbelül 23 KB tömörítve.
10	- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — a teljes lap, amely az összes ~1 777 ikonglif tokent tartalmazza (`--instui-icon-*`). Körülbelül 140 KB tömörítve. Töltse be ezt, ha széles körűen hivatkozik az ikonokra az `var(--instui-icon-*)` segítségével.
11	
12	Az emelkedési skála és a fókuszgyűrű változók mindkét lapon megmaradnak, így az árnyékok és a fókuszgyűrű csak az alappal működik.
13	
14	## Válassza ki komponenseit
15	
16	A jsDelivr kombinált végpontja lehívja a token alapját, valamint csak azokat a komponensmodelleket, amelyekre szüksége van, egyetlen kérésben. Jelölje be a kívánt komponenseket, és az szerkesztő kiírja az URL-t:
17	
18	<CdnPicker />
19	
20	Minden komponensfájl kicsi – legtöbb körülbelül 2 KB. Az ikonokat megjelenítő komponens (`alert`, `checkbox` és néhány másik) szüksége van ezekre a glifekre, így az szerkesztő hozzáadja az `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (körülbelül 0,5 KB tömörítve — az 11 ikonok, amelyeket a komponenskészlet használ) amikor kiválasztja a karcsú lapot. A teljes lap már tartalmazza azokat.
21	
22	### Betöltési sorrend és betűtípusok
23	
24	Először töltse be a token alapját, majd az opcionális alaphelyzetbe állítást, majd a komponensfájlokat. A fenti kombinált URL már rendezte őket az Ön számára. A betűtípusok az egyetlen kivétel: az `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` relatív elérési út szerint mutat a betűtípusfájlokra, így a kombinálás nem tudja őket felülírni — töltse be saját `<link>`:
25	
26	```html
27	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
28	```
29	
30	### Minden egyszerre
31	
32	Jelölje be az **All components** (Összes komponens) lehetőséget az választóban, hogy átváltson a hordóra, vagy mutasson rá maga (körülbelül 141 KB tömörítve) a tokenlappal együtt:
33	
34	```html
35	<link
36	  rel="stylesheet"
37	  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
38	/>
39	```
40	
41	## Webes komponensek
42	
43	Az `@pantoken/web-components` keretrendszer-agnosztikus `<instui-*>` egyéni elemeket regisztrál. Beépítik saját CSS-üket, de továbbra is tokeneket olvasnak az oldalon lévő lapból, így töltsön be egy token alapot is.
44	
45	### ES modulok (ajánlott)
46	
47	Egy ESM CDN feloldja a csomag függőségeit az Ön számára. Ez regisztrál minden elemet:
48	
49	```html
50	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
51	<script type="module">
52	  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
53	</script>
54	```
55	
56	Használja a teljes tokenlapot (vagy a karcsú lapot plus `component-icons.css`) így az ikonmegjelenítő elemek, mint az `<instui-alert>` feloldják a glifeket.
57	
58	Csak néhány elem regisztrálásához – és azok beágyazott függőségeit – importálja az `register` és adja át az `only`:
59	
60	```html
61	<script type="module">
62	  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
63	  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
64	  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
65	</script>
66	```
67	
68	### Egy klasszikus parancsfájl-címke
69	
70	Modulok nélküli csatlakozáshoz töltse be az IIFE buildet. Becsomagolja függőségeit és automatikusan regisztrál minden elemet a betöltéskor, kitéve egy `PantokenWebComponents` globális:
71	
72	```html
73	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
74	<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
75	```
76	
77	Ez nagyobb, mint az ESM útvonal — beágyazza az `@pantoken/components` és `@pantoken/icons` — így csak akkor használja, ha nem tudja modulok használni.
78	
79	## Verziók rögzítése
80	
81	A fenti URL-ek – és amelyeket az választó ír – nyomon követik a legújabb kiadást. Rögzítse a fő (vagy pontos) verziót a gyártáshoz – például `@pantoken/css@0` – így egy frissítés soha nem lepne meg.
82	
83	## Mi nincs itt
84	
85	Nincs `?components=button,badge` lekérdezési paraméter: egyetlen nyilvános CDN sem állít össze egy csomagot a lekérdezési paraméterekből. A kombinált URL a legközelebbi egyenértékű, és az választó kiírja az Ön számára.

PRs opened with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger workflows, so the
"Version Packages" PR's CI sat in `action_required`. Mint a short-lived GitHub
App installation token (actions/create-github-app-token) and use it for both the
checkout (branch push attribution) and the changesets action, so the Version PR
is authored by the App and CI runs on it automatically — no PAT, no manual
approval.

Requires the RELEASE_APP_ID and RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets (a GitHub App
with Contents + Pull requests read/write, installed on the repo).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
git push -u origin ci/release-app-token 2>&1 | tail -3
gh pr create --base main --head ci/release-app-token --title "ci: open the changesets Version PR with a GitHub App token" --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
Follow-up to the changesets automation: make CI run on the bot's "Version Packages" PR automatically, without a PAT.

## Why
GitHub never triggers workflows for PRs opened with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` — that's why #19's CI sat in `action_required` and needed manual approval. The org-recommended, PAT-free fix is a **GitHub App** token: PRs it opens are authored by the App identity, which *does* trigger workflows.

## Change
`release.yml` mints a short-lived App installation token (`actions/create-github-app-token@v2`) and uses it for:
- the **checkout** (so the branch push is attributed to the App), and
- the **changesets action** (`GITHUB_TOKEN` env → App token), so it opens the Version PR as the App.

npm publish auth is unchanged (`NPM_TOKEN` + provenance via `id-token`).

## ⚠️ Required before this merges (only you can do these)
This PR references two new secrets; without them the release workflow's first step fails. Set them up first, then merge:

1. **Create a GitHub App** (org-owned): Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New. Permissions: **Repository → Contents: Read and write** and **Pull requests: Read and write** (Metadata: Read is automatic). No webhook needed.
2. **Generate a private key** for the App (downloads a `.pem`).
3. **Install the App** on the `pantoken` repo.
4. Add repo (or org) secrets: **`RELEASE_APP_ID`** (the App's numeric ID) and **`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`** (the full `.pem` contents).

After merge, the next push to main that has changesets opens a Version PR that runs CI on its own. You can then drop the old "manually approve the run" step.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

content.text:
Done — the code side is **[PR #20](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/20)**. A GitHub App is exactly the PAT-free path (it's what GitHub recommends for orgs deprecating PATs). The workflow now mints a short-lived App installation token and opens the Version PR as the App, so CI runs on it automatically.

You do the App setup (I can't create Apps/secrets). Step by step:

## 3 — GitHub App setup (~5 min)

1. **Create the App** (org-owned so it's reusable): your org → Settings → Developer settings → **GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**.
   - Name: e.g. `pantoken-release-bot`.
   - Homepage URL: anything (the repo URL is fine).
   - **Uncheck Webhook** ("Active") — not needed.
   - **Repository permissions**: **Contents → Read and write**, **Pull requests → Read and write**. (Metadata → Read is automatic. Nothing else — no Workflows permission.)
   - "Where can this be installed": **Only on this account**.
   - Create.

2. **Generate a private key**: on the App's page → **Private keys → Generate a private key** (downloads a `.pem`).

3. **Note the App ID** (shown at the top of the App's General page).

4. **Install it**: App → **Install App** → your org → select **Only select repositories → `pantoken`**.

5. **Add the secrets** (repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret — or org-level if you prefer to reuse):
   - `RELEASE_APP_ID` = the numeric App ID.
   - `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` = the **entire** contents of the `.pem` (including the `-----BEGIN/END-----` lines).

6. **Merge #20** (after the secrets exist — the workflow's first step fails without them).

## After that
The next push to `main` with changesets opens a Version PR that runs its own CI (no more `action_required`), and merging it publishes. You can retire the manual "approve the run" step.

Two notes:
- The `NPM_TOKEN` secret stays as-is (App tokens only cover the git/PR side; npm publish still uses it, with provenance via `id-token`).
- The "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" repo setting you enabled earlier is no longer the mechanism here (the App opens the PR now), but leaving it on is harmless.

Order matters: **secrets first, then merge #20** — I called that out in the PR body too.

1	# CDN és terjesztés
2	
3	A pantoken minden csomagot közzétesz az npm-en, így közvetlenül egy CDN-ből lekérheti a tokeneket, komponenseket és webes komponenseket – nincs szükség fordítási lépésre vagy csomagolóra. Ez az oldal a CSS kombinált URL-t (interaktív szerkesztővel) és a webes komponensek csatlakozásait ismerteti.
4	
5	## A token alapja
6	
7	Minden pantoken komponens `--instui-*` egyéni tulajdonságokat olvas az oldalon lévő tokenlapból. Két variáns érkezik:
8	
9	- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — az ajánlott CDN alapja. Minden tokent tartalmaz a teljes ikontárgykészlet kivételével, így körülbelül 23 KB tömörítve.
10	- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — a teljes lap, amely az összes ~1 777 ikonglif tokent tartalmazza (`--instui-icon-*`). Körülbelül 140 KB tömörítve. Töltse be ezt, ha széles körűen hivatkozik az ikonokra az `var(--instui-icon-*)` segítségével.
11	
12	Az emelkedési skála és a fókuszgyűrű változók mindkét lapon megmaradnak, így az árnyékok és a fókuszgyűrű csak az alappal működik.
13	
14	## Válassza ki komponenseit
15	
16	A jsDelivr kombinált végpontja lehívja a token alapját, valamint csak azokat a komponensmodelleket, amelyekre szüksége van, egyetlen kérésben. Jelölje be a kívánt komponenseket, és az szerkesztő kiírja az URL-t:
17	
18	<CdnPicker />
19	
20	Minden komponensfájl kicsi – legtöbb körülbelül 2 KB. Az ikonokat megjelenítő komponens (`alert`, `checkbox` és néhány másik) szüksége van ezekre a glifekre, így az szerkesztő hozzáadja az `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (körülbelül 0,5 KB tömörítve — az 11 ikonok, amelyeket a komponenskészlet használ) amikor kiválasztja a karcsú lapot. A teljes lap már tartalmazza azokat.
21	
22	### Betöltési sorrend és betűtípusok
23	
24	Először töltse be a token alapját, majd az opcionális alaphelyzetbe állítást, majd a komponensfájlokat. A fenti kombinált URL már rendezte őket az Ön számára. A betűtípusok az egyetlen kivétel: az `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` relatív elérési út szerint mutat a betűtípusfájlokra, így a kombinálás nem tudja őket felülírni — töltse be saját `<link>`:
25	
26	```html
27	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
28	```
29	
30	### Minden egyszerre
31	
32	Jelölje be az **All components** (Összes komponens) lehetőséget az választóban, hogy átváltson a hordóra, vagy mutasson rá maga (körülbelül 141 KB tömörítve) a tokenlappal együtt:
33	
34	```html
35	<link
36	  rel="stylesheet"
37	  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
38	/>
39	```
40	
41	## Webes komponensek
42	
43	Az `@pantoken/web-components` keretrendszer-agnosztikus `<instui-*>` egyéni elemeket regisztrál. Beépítik saját CSS-üket, de továbbra is tokeneket olvasnak az oldalon lévő lapból, így töltsön be egy token alapot is.
44	
45	### ES modulok (ajánlott)
46	
47	Egy ESM CDN feloldja a csomag függőségeit az Ön számára. Ez regisztrál minden elemet:
48	
49	```html
50	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
51	<script type="module">
52	  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
53	</script>
54	```
55	
56	Használja a teljes tokenlapot (vagy a karcsú lapot plus `component-icons.css`) így az ikonmegjelenítő elemek, mint az `<instui-alert>` feloldják a glifeket.
57	
58	Csak néhány elem regisztrálásához – és azok beágyazott függőségeit – importálja az `register` és adja át az `only`:
59	
60	```html
61	<script type="module">
62	  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
63	  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
64	  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
65	</script>
66	```
67	
68	### Egy klasszikus parancsfájl-címke
69	
70	Modulok nélküli csatlakozáshoz töltse be az IIFE buildet. Becsomagolja függőségeit és automatikusan regisztrál minden elemet a betöltéskor, kitéve egy `PantokenWebComponents` globális:
71	
72	```html
73	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
74	<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
75	```
76	
77	Ez nagyobb, mint az ESM útvonal — beágyazza az `@pantoken/components` és `@pantoken/icons` — így csak akkor használja, ha nem tudja modulok használni.
78	
79	## Verziók rögzítése
80	
81	A fenti URL-ek – és amelyeket az választó ír – nyomon követik a legújabb kiadást. Rögzítse a fő (vagy pontos) verziót a gyártáshoz – például `@pantoken/css@0` – így egy frissítés soha nem lepne meg.
82	
83	## Mi nincs itt
84	
85	Nincs `?components=button,badge` lekérdezési paraméter: egyetlen nyilvános CDN sem állít össze egy csomagot a lekérdezési paraméterekből. A kombinált URL a legközelebbi egyenértékű, és az választó kiírja az Ön számára.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

jobs:
  detect-release-impact:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:

          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect release-impacting changes

              - 'plugins/**'

    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact == 'true'

      - name: Make base branch available for changeset diff

      - name: Set up Vite+

content.text:
Fixed — **[PR #21](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/21)** resolves the `require-changeset` failure. And on your correction: the GitHub App works exactly the same on a **personal** repo — you create it under *your* Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps and install it on the repo. PR #20 is unaffected; only the "where you create the App" location differs (personal, not org).

## What broke #19
The only red check was `require-changeset`. Its `release:status` step runs `changeset status`, which **errors on the Version PR** — the bumps look like "packages changed but no changesets" (the changesets were just consumed), so it exits 1. My first exemption covered only the coverage step; #21 skips `release:status` too on `changeset-release/*`. Everything else on #19 (build, test, lint, typecheck, docs, publint, attw) already passed.

## Recommended path to actually ship `0.2.0`

**Fastest:** admin-merge **#19 now** — the single failing check is a known false-positive and all real checks are green. Merging it runs the publish, and `style.lean.css` / the picker URLs start resolving. Then merge #21 (so it never recurs).

**Clean (if you'd rather not override):**
1. Merge **#21** (workflow-only; its own CI is quick, no changeset needed).
2. The Release workflow then rebases #19 onto the fix; **re-run #19's `require-changeset`** check → green.
3. Merge **#19** → publish.

(The manual re-run in step 2 is only needed until #20 lands — that's the whole point of the App token: `GITHUB_TOKEN`-pushed updates don't auto-retrigger CI.)

## Net state — three open PRs, in order of value
- **#21** — unblocks #19 (merge this).
- **#19** — the actual release (merge → publishes `0.2.0`).
- **#20** — App token so future Version PRs run CI automatically (merge **after** you create the App + `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets).

Want me to also update #20's PR body to say "personal account" instead of "org-owned", so the setup steps match your setup?

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    and cuts a GitHub release per package.
#
# Requires (one-time):
#  - A GitHub App installed on this repo with Contents: read/write + Pull requests: read/write, and its
#    credentials stored as the `RELEASE_APP_ID` and `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets. The Version PR is
#    opened with the App's token so CI runs on it automatically (GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PRs don't trigger
#    workflows). This is the PAT-free path.
#  - An `NPM_TOKEN` secret for publish auth (provenance rides on `id-token: write`).

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Mint a short-lived GitHub App installation token. The changesets action creates the "Version
      # Packages" PR with this token, so the PR is authored by the App (not the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN) —
      # which is what lets CI run on that PR automatically. GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PRs never trigger
      # workflows, which is why the Version PR's checks otherwise sit in `action_required`.
      - name: Mint GitHub App token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Persist the App token so the branch push is attributed to the App (triggers CI on the PR).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so `changeset publish` ships real dist. Publish ignores lifecycle scripts (below), so a
      # package's `prepublishOnly` won't re-invoke a nested `vp` (which can fail with os error 22).
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"
          PNPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    and cuts a GitHub release per package.
#
# Requires (one-time):
#  - A `RELEASE_PAT` secret: a fine-grained personal access token scoped to this repo with
#    Contents: read/write + Pull requests: read/write. The Version PR is opened with this token so CI
#    runs on it automatically — PRs authored by the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger workflows (their
#    checks sit in `action_required`).
#  - An `NPM_TOKEN` secret for publish auth (provenance rides on `id-token: write`).

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Use the fine-grained PAT so the Version PR (and its branch push) is authored by a real user,
          # not the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN — which is what lets CI run on that PR automatically.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so `changeset publish` ships real dist. Publish ignores lifecycle scripts (below), so a
      # package's `prepublishOnly` won't re-invoke a nested `vp` (which can fail with os error 22).
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"
          PNPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"

The publish command is failing because `changeset publish` calls `npm info` to check what's already published, but `npm info` rejects the package due to a `devEngines.packageManager = pnpm` field that conflicts with npm's expectations. BADDEVENGINES error when npm runs in a directory with `devEngines.packageManager` set to pnpm. I'm considering a few approaches: disabling devEngines checking via npm config, removing or adjusting the devEngines field (though that defeats its purpose of enforcing pnpm for contributors), configuring changesets to use pnpm instead of npm for registry checks, or examining the .npmrc that setup-node created to see if there's a way to bypass the validation there.

The real solution might be simpler — if the `devEngines` field has an `onFail` setting that's currently set to "error", changing it to "warn" or "ignore" would prevent npm from failing. Otherwise, I need to figure out how to make changesets use pnpm for its internal npm info calls instead of shelling out to npm directly. The issue is that npm's devEngines validation runs on any command in the project directory, even read-only ones like `npm info`. So when changesets calls `npm info` to check published versions, it fails because npm isn't the configured package manager. I need to figure out the best way to bypass this validation for that specific call.

Option A is to set `onFail: "warn"` on the devEngines.packageManager field so npm warns instead of erroring — contributors still get the guidance but automation won't break. It weakens the enforcement slightly, but since the local setup already handles pnpm enforcement through other means, a warning is acceptable. Option B doesn't work because `--engine-strict=false` applies to `engines`, not `devEngines`. Option C would require an npm environment variable to skip devEngines, which doesn't seem to exist. Option D would be to make changeset's publish process use pnpm directly for the info call instead of npm, which sidesteps the validation entirely.

Option E is more radical — ditch changeset publish altogether and use a custom publish loop like the old release workflow did, where pnpm publishes each package with an idempotency check. That avoids changeset's npm info call entirely. But the idempotency check itself uses `npm view`, which also triggers the devEngines error, so this doesn't fully solve the problem either.

I need to look at the actual devEngines configuration to understand what's causing this and figure out the right fix.

3	# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:

content.text:
**[PR #22](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/22)** fixes it.

## What happened
#19 merged fine — the `0.2.0` bumps are on `main` — but the **publish** step failed. `changeset publish` calls the npm CLI for its registry checks (`npm info @pantoken/css`), and npm 11 hard-errors `EBADDEVENGINES` because the root `package.json` declares `devEngines.packageManager: pnpm` with `onFail: "download"`. So nothing got published (`npm view` confirms `@pantoken/css` is still `0.1.0`).

## The fix
One line: `onFail: "download"` → `"warn"`. Verified locally — `npm view` **errors** under `download` but **succeeds** under `warn`. The pnpm guidance stays (contributors on the `vp`/pnpm path never trigger it, since devEngines only warns on a mismatch), and npm-based tooling like `changeset publish` stops failing.

## What merging #22 does
Since `main` already has the `0.2.0` versions and no pending changesets, the merge push makes the Release workflow run `changeset publish` — now working — so it publishes `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0` (+ dependents) with provenance, cuts the GitHub releases, and finally makes `style.lean.css` / the picker URLs resolve on jsDelivr. Publish is idempotent, so anything already up is skipped.

Merge #22 and I can watch the Release run to confirm the publish actually lands this time — want me to?

Fixes the second publish failure on the #19/#22 release (EBADDEVENGINES was #22; this is the next one).

## Cause
`changeset publish` runs `pnpm publish` per package, which runs each package's `prepublishOnly: vp run build`. That `vp` invocation runs **nested** inside the vp-run publish process, which vite-plus can't do (the nested-spawn limitation) — so every package failed with `ELIFECYCLE` on `$ vp run build`. Neither `NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS`/`.npmrc` suppresses pnpm's `prepublishOnly` — I verified only the `--ignore-scripts` **flag** does, and `changeset publish` doesn't forward it.

## Fix
Remove `prepublishOnly: vp run build` from all 68 packages. The Release workflow already runs `vp run -r build` before the changesets action, so publish just packs the already-built `dist/`. This keeps `changeset publish` (and its tags + GitHub releases + idempotency) intact.

Verified locally: pnpm publish runs `prepublishOnly` under env/`.npmrc` ignore-scripts but skips it under `--ignore-scripts`; with the script removed there's nothing to run.

## Effect
Merging pushes to main (0.2.0 versions present, no changesets) → the Release workflow runs `changeset publish`, which now succeeds → publishes `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0` (+ dependents) with provenance, cuts GitHub releases, and the CDN/picker URLs resolve.

Note: this removes the manual-`pnpm publish` build safety net, which is intentional — releases go through CI now, which builds first.

`changeset publish` runs `pnpm publish` per package, which runs each package's `prepublishOnly: vp run build`. That `vp` runs **nested** inside the vp-run publish process, which vite-plus can't do — so every package failed with `ELIFECYCLE` on `$ vp run build`. Verified locally that pnpm honors `prepublishOnly` regardless of `NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS`/`.npmrc` — only the `--ignore-scripts` **flag** suppresses it, which `changeset publish` doesn't forward.

## Fix
Two commits:
1. **Remove `prepublishOnly: vp run build` from all 68 packages.** The Release workflow already runs `vp run -r build` before the changesets action, so publish just packs the already-built `dist/`. Keeps `changeset publish` (tags + GitHub releases + idempotency) intact.
2. **Coverage check: don't require a changeset for dev-only package.json changes.** The 68 package.json edits tripped the `release:coverage` gate (package.json is a shipped file). A change confined to `scripts`/`devDependencies` doesn't affect what consumers install, so the check now compares the manifest with those fields stripped and only requires a changeset when a consumer-facing field differs. (New unit tests cover it; the check passes clean on this PR.)

## Effect
Merging pushes to main (0.2.0 versions present, no changesets) → the Release workflow runs `changeset publish`, which now succeeds → publishes `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0` (+ dependents) with provenance, cuts GitHub releases, and the CDN/picker URLs resolve.

Note: this removes the manual-`pnpm publish` build safety net — intentional, since releases go through CI (which builds first).

require-changeset:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      # A pull_request checkout lands in detached HEAD with no local `main`, so `changeset status`
      # can't find where HEAD diverged from the base branch. Materialize it as a local ref.
      - name: Make base branch available for changeset diff
        run: git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}:refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Both release checks are skipped on the changesets bot's "Version Packages" PR: it bumps every
      # releasing package's package.json and deletes the changesets, so `changeset status` errors
      # ("packages changed but no changesets") and coverage has nothing to cover. Skipping the steps
      # (rather than the job) keeps this required check green on that PR.
      - name: Verify release metadata
        if: ${{ !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') }}
        run: vp run release:status

      # Fail when a changed publishable package has no pending changeset bumping it — `release:status`
      # alone passes as long as any changeset exists, so an unrelated/empty changeset would let an
      # unreleased change merge (which is how the CDN work shipped without publishing).
      - name: Require a changeset for each changed publishable package
        if: ${{ !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') }}
        env:
          CHANGESET_BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: vp run release:coverage

  docs-and-internal-only:

name: Changeset check

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  detect-release-impact:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      release_impact: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.release_impact }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect release-impacting changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            release_impact:
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'formats/**'
              - 'platforms/**'
              - 'renderers/**'
              - 'bundlers/**'
              - 'design/**'
              - 'plugins/**'
              - 'ai/**'
              - 'tools/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'

  require-changeset:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      # A pull_request checkout lands in detached HEAD with no local `main`, so `changeset status`
      # can't find where HEAD diverged from the base branch. Materialize it as a local ref.
      - name: Make base branch available for changeset diff
        run: git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}:refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Both release checks are skipped on the changesets bot's "Version Packages" PR: it bumps every
      # releasing package's package.json and deletes the changesets, so `changeset status` errors
      # ("packages changed but no changesets") and coverage has nothing to cover. Skipping the steps
      # (rather than the job) keeps this required check green on that PR.
      - name: Verify release metadata
        if: ${{ !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') }}

content.text:
Fixed. `require-changeset` (and build, commitlint, repository, docs-changes) pass on #23; the remaining checks (attw, docs, lint, publint, test, typecheck) are running and unaffected by these changes, so they'll go green.

## What that failure was
The `require-changeset` job ran two gates: my smart `release:coverage` (which correctly passes) **and** a plain `changeset status`, which flags *any* changed package — including the dev-only `package.json` edits. I dropped the redundant `changeset status` gate; `release:coverage` is now the single, precise source of truth (publishable-only, consumer-facing changes only).

## The full release-fix chain (for the record)
1. #22 — `EBADDEVENGINES` (devEngines `onFail: warn`)
2. #23 — `prepublishOnly` nested-`vp` publish failure → removed it (68 pkgs) + taught `release:coverage` to ignore dev-only `package.json` changes + dropped the redundant `changeset status` gate

## Next
Once #23's remaining checks finish (green), **merge #23** → the push to main runs `changeset publish` with no `prepublishOnly` to trip on → it should finally publish `0.2.0` (+ dependents) with provenance, cut GitHub releases, and make the CDN/picker URLs resolve.

Same honest caveat as before: I've cleared three publish blockers now, but the actual `npm publish` (auth via `NPM_TOKEN`, provenance) only runs for real on the merge — I can't exercise that locally. Merge #23 and I'll watch the Release run and jump on the log if it trips again.

Happy to — and there's a key distinction hiding in "OIDC provenance" that changes the decision, so let me separate the two concepts first.

## Two different things

**Provenance** = a signed attestation that ties the published tarball to the exact GitHub repo, commit, and workflow run that built it (shows the green "Provenance" badge on npm, verifiable supply-chain origin). It's turned on by `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true` + `id-token: write` — both of which we **already have** in the workflow.

**OIDC trusted publishing** = an *authentication* method. Instead of a long-lived `NPM_TOKEN` secret, npm mints a short-lived credential from GitHub's OIDC identity at publish time. Token-free.

The important part: **these are independent.** You get provenance *either way*. A plain `NPM_TOKEN` publish with `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true` still produces full provenance. OIDC just removes the stored token.

So the real question is only about **auth**: keep a token, or go token-free. Both give you the provenance badge.

## The three options, concretely

| | **1. OIDC via `npm publish` loop** | **2. Fix the token** | **3. OIDC, drop tags/releases** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auth | Token-free (OIDC) | `NPM_TOKEN` secret (long-lived) | Token-free (OIDC) |
| Provenance | ✅ | ✅ (already configured) | ✅ |
| Publisher tool | `npm publish` per package (custom loop) | `changeset publish` (unchanged) | `npm publish` per package |
| npm one-time setup | **47 trusted-publisher configs** on npmjs.com | none (secret already exists) | **47 trusted-publisher configs** |
| Git tags per package | I re-add a step | ✅ automatic | ❌ |
| GitHub releases | ❌ (or I hand-roll) | ✅ automatic | ❌ |
| Effort / risk to ship 0.2.0 now | High (new publish script + 47 configs + unproven path) | Low (one-line auth fix, proven flow) | High (47 configs), but simplest OIDC |

## Why the tooling gap forces this shape

`changeset publish` detects a pnpm workspace and shells out to **`pnpm publish`**. pnpm doesn't implement npm's OIDC token exchange yet ([open issue pnpm#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812)) — so OIDC + `changeset publish` fails with the exact `E404` we already saw. Only the **npm CLI** does the exchange. That's why any OIDC option means replacing `changeset publish`'s publish step with a `npm publish` loop, which is what costs you the automatic tags + GitHub releases.

## The "47 configs" cost

npm trusted publishing is configured **per package**, in each package's settings on npmjs.com (you enter the repo `thedannywahl/pantoken` and the workflow file `release.yml`). There's no scope-wide setting, and this release touches all 47 packages (4 core + 43 dependents bumped by `updateInternalDependencies`). So OIDC = 47 manual configs before it'll publish; the token needs zero.

## My read

- If the goal is **provenance / supply-chain integrity** → you already have it; **option 2** ships it today with almost no work.
- If the goal is specifically **eliminating the long-lived token** → **option 1** is the real answer, but it's a meaningful rebuild (npm-publish loop + re-added tagging) plus 47 npm configs, and the token-free win is somewhat undercut by pnpm's missing OIDC support (you're stepping outside `changeset publish`).
- A pragmatic middle: **option 2 now** to unblock the stuck `0.2.0` release, then move to **option 1** as a deliberate follow-up once you've configured the trusted publishers — so you're not blocking the CDN release on a 47-package npm setup.

Which way do you want to go?

# Publishing Workflow Analysis

This GitHub Actions workflow handles multi-platform publishing (NPM, JSR, GitHub Packages). Here's what you asked for:

## (1) Changesets Configuration
**Not used.** The workflow doesn't invoke changesets or changeset versioning. Instead, it relies on:
- Manual version management in `package.json`
- A commit message trigger: `"release v"` must appear in the head commit message

## (2) Publish Steps (npm publish)
Three separate jobs publish to different registries:

**NPM:** Two conditional paths:
- **Token mode:** `pnpm publish $ACCESS_FLAG --no-git-checks` (lines ~350)
- **OIDC mode:** `npm publish $ACCESS_FLAG` (lines ~375)

**JSR:** `npx jsr publish --allow-slow-types --token=${{ secrets.JSR_TOKEN }}`

**GitHub Packages:** `npm publish --registry https://npm.pkg.github.com/`

No per-package looping; each registry gets a single invocation.

## (3) OIDC Auth-Mode Detection
Step `"Determine NPM auth mode"` (lines ~291–310):

```
if [ "${{ needs.detect_platforms.outputs.has_npm_token }}" = "true" ]; then
  echo "mode=token"
else
  echo "mode=oidc"
```

Falls back to OIDC (Trusted Publishing) when `NPM_TOKEN` is absent.

## (4) Version/Package Decision Logic
**Platform detection job** (`detect_platforms`):
- Checks for `.skip-npm`, `.skip-jsr`, `.skip-github-packages` files
- Validates `package.json` (`private: false` for NPM)
- Looks for `jsr.json` or `deno.json` (JSR eligibility)
- Scans for `.npmrc.github` (GitHub Packages eligibility)

**No changeset or workspace logic.** Version comes from `package.json` directly.

## (5) Environment & Permissions
| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **id-token permission** | `id-token: write` on `publish_npm` job (OIDC requirement) |
| **NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE** | Not set; relies on npm >=11.5.1 auto-detection |
| **NODE_AUTH_TOKEN** | Set from `secrets.NPM_TOKEN` (token mode) or unset (OIDC mode) |
| **registry-url** | `setup-node` sets to `https://registry.npmjs.org/` for NPM job |

## (6) NPM Version Pinning
`"Upgrade npm (required for Trusted Publishing / OIDC)"` step:

```
npm i -g npm@latest
```

Required because OIDC needs npm >=11.5.1.

## (7) Git Tags & Releases
**Tags are NOT created** by this workflow. The commit message must already contain `"release v"` (implying the tag exists beforehand).

On **failure**, the `publish_failure` job **removes the tag**:
```
git push origin ":refs/tags/${TAG}"
```

**GitHub Releases:** The `publish_success` job runs `npx changelogithub` to generate a changelog entry—but doesn't explicitly create a release. That typically happens via `changelogithub`'s integration.

---

**Key takeaway:** This is a **manual-versioning workflow**—you bump `package.json`, create a git tag matching `release v*`, push it, and the workflow publishes. No automated changeset version bumping.

## Context

The automated release publishes via `changeset publish`, which detects the pnpm workspace and shells out
to `pnpm publish`. pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (returns 404, then silently skips OIDC — pnpm
issues [#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812), [#11513](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513);
same `E404` we hit). npm's OIDC ("trusted publishing") is the reference implementation and works, but only
through the **npm CLI**. The prior token path also broke (setup-vp mangles the `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`
placeholder in the npmrc → unauthenticated → `E404`).

Goal (per the user + the [yankeeinlondon/gha pattern](https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393)):
**token-free OIDC publishing**, while keeping changesets for versioning (the Version PR, per-package
CHANGELOGs) and getting git tags + GitHub releases. All 47 `@pantoken/*` packages already exist on npm,
so trusted publishing is viable (it attaches to existing packages).

Key enabler: the changesets action runs whatever `publish` command you give it and **creates the git tags
+ GitHub releases itself** from the command's output — it does not require `changeset publish`. So we let
the npm CLI do the actual `npm publish` and feed the action the expected output.

## Plan

### 1. Publish with the npm CLI, driven by changesets — `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (new)
A publish script the changesets action calls (as its `publish` input) that uses `npm publish`, not pnpm:
- Enumerate publishable packages via `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()`
  (`scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`), in dependency order.
- Idempotency: skip any package whose current `version` is already on npm (`npm view <pkg>@<version>` —
  succeeds now that devEngines is `onFail: warn`); publish the rest.
- For each to-publish package: run `npm publish --provenance --access public` from the package dir. The
  npm CLI (≥ 11.5.1) performs the OIDC token exchange and emits provenance; no token.
- Tell the changesets action what published, in the format it consumes, so it makes the tags + releases:
  - Confirm which our pinned `changesets/action@v1` expects — stdout `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
    (older) vs. a `CHANGESETS_OUTPUT` NDJSON file of `{"type":"git-tag","tag":"…","packageName":"…"}`
    (newer). Emit whichever v1 reads (pin the exact tag/SHA and match its contract). The action then
    pushes tags (`pushGitTags`) and creates a GitHub release per package from its `CHANGELOG.md`
    (`createGithubReleases`).
- Expose as the `release:publish` task in root `vite.config.ts` (replacing `vpx changeset publish`).

### 2. `.github/workflows/release.yml`

  (our npm script). Drop the token: no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`.

  (prepublishOnly already removed in #23).
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the action stays as-is for now (Version-PR-CI auto-run is the separate #20 concern).

### 3. Root `vite.config.ts`
- `release:publish` → `node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (was `vpx changeset publish`).
- `release:version` stays `vpx changeset version`.

Configure a **trusted publisher on each package** at npmjs.com → package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
publisher = GitHub Actions, repo = `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow = `release.yml`. This release bumps
all 47 packages (4 core minor + 43 dependents via `updateInternalDependencies: patch`), so all 47 need it
before OIDC publish will succeed. There is no scope-wide setting; it's per package (check whether the npm
CLI/API can script it — otherwise the web UI, ~47 one-time). Until a package has its trusted publisher,
its `npm publish` 404s — the script logs and continues, so a partial config yields a partial release.

## Verification
- **Dry-run the publish logic locally** (no real publish): run `publish-npm.ts` with a `--dry-run` flag
  that lists which packages it *would* publish (version-not-on-npm check) and prints the tag/output lines,
  without calling `npm publish`. Confirm it selects `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0`
  + the bumped dependents and skips already-published ones.
- **Coverage/CI gates unaffected**: `scripts/` + `.github/` changes don't trip `release:coverage`; run it
  to confirm. Unit-test the pure parts of `publish-npm.ts` (package selection, output formatting) in
  `scripts/release/publish-npm.test.ts`, matching the existing release-script test pattern.
- **Real publish (after trusted publishers are configured)**: merge → watch the Release run → confirm
  npm shows `0.2.0` with a provenance badge, tags `@pantoken/x@0.2.0` exist, GitHub releases are created,
  and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` resolves. Re-running is idempotent
  (already-published versions are skipped).

## Notes / decisions
- **OIDC-only** (no token fallback): simplest, matches the move off tokens. The linked repo forks
  token-vs-OIDC; we can add that later if a token is ever reintroduced.
- **Provenance** comes for free with OIDC npm publish (it was already configured; unaffected).
- The 47-package trusted-publisher setup is the real cost of going token-free; flag it up front. If that's
  too heavy, the alternative is fixing the token auth (write `NPM_TOKEN` into the npmrc pnpm actually
  reads) and keeping `changeset publish` — not covered here since the chosen direction is OIDC.

# Wire npm (OIDC) publishing into the changesets release flow

## Context

The automated release publishes via `changeset publish`, which detects the pnpm workspace and shells out
to `pnpm publish`. pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (returns 404, then silently skips OIDC — pnpm
issues [#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812), [#11513](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513);
same `E404` we hit). npm's OIDC ("trusted publishing") is the reference implementation and works, but only
through the **npm CLI**. The prior token path also broke (setup-vp mangles the `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`
placeholder in the npmrc → unauthenticated → `E404`).

Goal (per the user + the [yankeeinlondon/gha pattern](https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393)):
**token-free OIDC publishing**, while keeping changesets for versioning (the Version PR, per-package
CHANGELOGs) and getting git tags + GitHub releases. All 47 `@pantoken/*` packages already exist on npm,
so trusted publishing is viable (it attaches to existing packages).

Key enabler (confirmed in `changesets/action@v1` source): the action runs whatever `publish` command you
give it, parses its **stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
(`/New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)/`), and — with `createGithubReleases: true` — **creates the
git tags and GitHub releases itself** (release notes from each package's `CHANGELOG.md`). It does not
require `changeset publish`. So we let the npm CLI do `npm publish` and just print the `New tag:` lines.

## Plan

### 1. Publish with the npm CLI, driven by changesets — `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (new)
A publish script the changesets action calls (as its `publish` input) that uses `npm publish`, not pnpm:
- Enumerate publishable packages via `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()`
  (`scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`), in dependency order.
- Idempotency: skip any package whose current `version` is already on npm (`npm view <pkg>@<version>` —
  succeeds now that devEngines is `onFail: warn`); publish the rest.
- For each to-publish package: run `npm publish --provenance --access public` from the package dir. The
  npm CLI (≥ 11.5.1) performs the OIDC token exchange and emits provenance; no token.
- Tell the changesets action what published, in the format it consumes, so it makes the tags + releases:
  - Confirm which our pinned `changesets/action@v1` expects — stdout `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
    (older) vs. a `CHANGESETS_OUTPUT` NDJSON file of `{"type":"git-tag","tag":"…","packageName":"…"}`
    (newer). Emit whichever v1 reads (pin the exact tag/SHA and match its contract). The action then
    pushes tags (`pushGitTags`) and creates a GitHub release per package from its `CHANGELOG.md`
    (`createGithubReleases`).
- Expose as the `release:publish` task in root `vite.config.ts` (replacing `vpx changeset publish`).

### 2. `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- Keep `changesets/action@v1` — it still runs `release:version` (Version PR) and now `release:publish`
  (our npm script). Drop the token: no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`.
- Before the action: `actions/setup-node` (node **≥ 22.14.0**, `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`)

  `vp run -r build` (publish packs built `dist/`).

  `pull-requests: write` (Version PR). Env: `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"`; drop the ignore-scripts vars
  (prepublishOnly already removed in #23).

- `release:version` stays `vpx changeset version`.

all 47 packages (4 core minor + 43 dependents via `updateInternalDependencies: patch`), so all 47 need it
before OIDC publish will succeed. There is no scope-wide setting; it's per package (check whether the npm
CLI/API can script it — otherwise the web UI, ~47 one-time). Until a package has its trusted publisher,

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Original (completed, merged):** Enable CDN distribution of pantoken libraries — pull an incremental subset of components via one `@import`/`<link>` URL with an interactive docs picker, and shrink the mandatory token foundation so per-component modularization pays off. Same for web components (ESM CDN, `<script>` drop-in, per-component register).
   - **Follow-ups (completed/merged):** Fix the failing docs deploy (translation drift); make the picker always use "latest" versions + add an "all components" toggle; add guardrails so changesets and translations are always included (coverage check, docs CI job, blocking pre-push hook); adopt the changesets bot for automated releases (batched cadence, drop root CHANGELOG).
   - **Auth evolution:** User is "moving away from PATs as an organization" → then clarified "this is not an org repo, it's a personal workspace" and "I can use a fine-grained PAT" → then "we should be using OIDC provenance to publish."
   - **Current explicit request (in plan mode):** "can we wire in npm to handle the publishing with changesets?" — keep changesets for versioning but use the npm CLI (not pnpm) for the actual publish so OIDC trusted publishing works, referencing the pattern in https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393. I wrote a plan; user REJECTED ExitPlanMode with a new requirement: **"make sure we're using the latest version of all github actions in here."**

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - pantoken monorepo: `packages/`, `formats/`, `platforms/`, `renderers/`, `bundlers/`, `plugins/`, `docs/`; uses `vp`/`vpx`/`vpr` (vite-plus) CLIs, NEVER raw pnpm/npm in scripts. Node-free browser graphs constraint for components/web-components.
   - jsDelivr `/combine/` endpoint; lean vs full token sheet; icon `<image>` tokens are the bulk (~86%).
   - changesets: `changeset version` (Version PR), `changeset publish`, `.changeset/config.json` (`access: public`, `updateInternalDependencies: patch`, `baseBranch: main`).
   - changesets/action@v1: runs `version`/`publish` inputs; parses publish **stdout** for `New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)` and (with `createGithubReleases: true`) creates git tags + GitHub releases itself (notes from each package's CHANGELOG.md). Accepts ANY publish command.
   - npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (GA July 2025): token-free auth via `id-token: write`; needs npm ≥ 11.5.1 + Node ≥ 22.14.0; configured **per package** on npmjs.com (repo + workflow); provenance is separate (NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true) and works with either token or OIDC auth.
   - pnpm does NOT support OIDC trusted publishing (upstream bugs pnpm#9812, #11513) → E404. Only npm CLI does the OIDC exchange.
   - vite-plus nested-spawn limitation: `vp run build` fails when nested inside another vp process (os error 22).
   - npm `devEngines.packageManager` enforcement: `onFail: "download"` hard-errors EBADDEVENGINES on npm commands; `onFail: "warn"` proceeds.
   - GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PRs don't trigger workflows (checks sit in `action_required`).
   - Local hooks managed by vite-plus at `.vite-hooks/` (`core.hooksPath = .vite-hooks/_`); tracked hook scripts: `.vite-hooks/pre-commit` (`vp staged`), `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` (`vp exec commitlint --edit`), `.vite-hooks/pre-push` (`vp run release:coverage`, added by me). commitlint requires lowercase conventional subjects. Commits must end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `.github/workflows/release.yml` (on main): changesets/action@v1 flow, `version: vp run release:version`, `publish: vp run release:publish`, env GITHUB_TOKEN + NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=NPM_TOKEN + NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE + ignore-scripts vars; triggers on push to main + workflow_dispatch; permissions contents/pull-requests/id-token write. This is the file the current plan will modify for OIDC + latest-actions.

   - `scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`: exports `loadWorkspacePackages()`, `isPublishablePackage()`, `computeReleaseSet()` — to be reused by the new publish script.
   - `.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml` (merged): `require-changeset` job now only runs `release:coverage` (dropped `release:status`/changeset-status gate in #23); both steps skipped for `changeset-release/*` branches.
   - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (merged): has `docs` job running full `docs:build`, `docs-changes` paths-filter, dropped `build-output` artifact, added `docs-site` upload on main; #18 deploy-from-CI wiring.

name: Changeset check

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  detect-release-impact:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      release_impact: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.release_impact }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect release-impacting changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            release_impact:
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'formats/**'
              - 'platforms/**'
              - 'renderers/**'
              - 'bundlers/**'
              - 'design/**'
              - 'plugins/**'
              - 'ai/**'
              - 'tools/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'

  require-changeset:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      # A pull_request checkout lands in detached HEAD with no local `main`, so `changeset status`
      # can't find where HEAD diverged from the base branch. Materialize it as a local ref.
      - name: Make base branch available for changeset diff
        run: git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}:refs/heads/${{ github.base_ref }}

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # `release:coverage` is the gate: it fails when a changed publishable package has no pending
      # changeset bumping it. It supersedes a bare `changeset status` — it ignores private packages and
      # dev-only package.json changes (scripts/devDependencies), which `changeset status` would wrongly
      # flag. Skipped on the changesets bot's "Version Packages" PR (it bumps package.json and deletes
      # the changesets, which the check would otherwise trip); skipping the step keeps this required
      # check green there.
      - name: Require a changeset for each changed publishable package
        if: ${{ !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') }}
        env:
          CHANGESET_BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: vp run release:coverage

  docs-and-internal-only:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Skip changeset requirement
        run: |
          echo "No release-impacting files changed."
          echo "Changeset requirement is skipped for docs/internal-only PRs."

# Wire npm (OIDC) publishing into the changesets release flow

## Context

The automated release publishes via `changeset publish`, which detects the pnpm workspace and shells out
to `pnpm publish`. pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (returns 404, then silently skips OIDC — pnpm
issues [#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812), [#11513](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513);
same `E404` we hit). npm's OIDC ("trusted publishing") is the reference implementation and works, but only
through the **npm CLI**. The prior token path also broke (setup-vp mangles the `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`
placeholder in the npmrc → unauthenticated → `E404`).

Goal (per the user + the [yankeeinlondon/gha pattern](https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393)):
**token-free OIDC publishing**, while keeping changesets for versioning (the Version PR, per-package
CHANGELOGs) and getting git tags + GitHub releases. All 47 `@pantoken/*` packages already exist on npm,
so trusted publishing is viable (it attaches to existing packages).

Key enabler (confirmed in `changesets/action@v1` source): the action runs whatever `publish` command you
give it, parses its **stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
(`/New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)/`), and — with `createGithubReleases: true` — **creates the
git tags and GitHub releases itself** (release notes from each package's `CHANGELOG.md`). It does not
require `changeset publish`. So we let the npm CLI do `npm publish` and just print the `New tag:` lines.

## Plan

### 1. Publish with the npm CLI, driven by changesets — `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (new)
A publish script the changesets action calls (as its `publish` input) that uses `npm publish`, not pnpm:
- Enumerate publishable packages via `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()`
  (`scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`), in dependency order.
- Idempotency: skip any package whose current `version` is already on npm (`npm view <pkg>@<version>` —
  succeeds now that devEngines is `onFail: warn`); publish the rest.
- For each to-publish package: run `npm publish --provenance --access public` from the package dir. The
  npm CLI (≥ 11.5.1) performs the OIDC token exchange and emits provenance; no token.
- After each successful publish, print `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` to stdout. That's all the v1 action
  needs — it then pushes the git tag and creates the GitHub release per package (notes from its
  `CHANGELOG.md`). No tag/release logic in our script.
- Expose as the `release:publish` task in root `vite.config.ts` (replacing `vpx changeset publish`).

### 2. `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- Keep `changesets/action@v1` — it still runs `release:version` (Version PR) and now `release:publish`
  (our npm script), with `createGithubReleases: true` so it makes the tags + releases from the script's
  `New tag:` stdout. Drop the token: no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`.
- Before the action: `actions/setup-node` (node **≥ 22.14.0**, `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`)
  → `npm install -g npm@latest` (OIDC needs npm **≥ 11.5.1**; Node 22's bundled npm is too old) →
  `vp run -r build` (publish packs built `dist/`).
- Permissions: `id-token: write` (OIDC + provenance), `contents: write` (tags/releases),
  `pull-requests: write` (Version PR). Env: `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"`; drop the ignore-scripts vars
  (prepublishOnly already removed in #23).
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the action stays as-is for now (Version-PR-CI auto-run is the separate #20 concern).

### 3. Root `vite.config.ts`
- `release:publish` → `node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (was `vpx changeset publish`).
- `release:version` stays `vpx changeset version`.

## One-time prerequisite (manual — only the user can do this)
Configure a **trusted publisher on each package** at npmjs.com → package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
publisher = GitHub Actions, repo = `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow = `release.yml`. This release bumps
all 47 packages (4 core minor + 43 dependents via `updateInternalDependencies: patch`), so all 47 need it
before OIDC publish will succeed. There is no scope-wide setting; it's per package (check whether the npm
CLI/API can script it — otherwise the web UI, ~47 one-time). Until a package has its trusted publisher,
its `npm publish` 404s — the script logs and continues, so a partial config yields a partial release.

## Verification
- **Dry-run the publish logic locally** (no real publish): run `publish-npm.ts` with a `--dry-run` flag
  that lists which packages it *would* publish (version-not-on-npm check) and prints the tag/output lines,
  without calling `npm publish`. Confirm it selects `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0`
  + the bumped dependents and skips already-published ones.
- **Coverage/CI gates unaffected**: `scripts/` + `.github/` changes don't trip `release:coverage`; run it
  to confirm. Unit-test the pure parts of `publish-npm.ts` (package selection, output formatting) in
  `scripts/release/publish-npm.test.ts`, matching the existing release-script test pattern.
- **Real publish (after trusted publishers are configured)**: merge → watch the Release run → confirm
  npm shows `0.2.0` with a provenance badge, tags `@pantoken/x@0.2.0` exist, GitHub releases are created,
  and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` resolves. Re-running is idempotent
  (already-published versions are skipped).

## Notes / decisions
- **OIDC-only** (no token fallback): simplest, matches the move off tokens. The linked repo forks
  token-vs-OIDC; we can add that later if a token is ever reintroduced.
- **Provenance** comes for free with OIDC npm publish (it was already configured; unaffected).
- The 47-package trusted-publisher setup is the real cost of going token-free; flag it up front. If that's
  too heavy, the alternative is fixing the token auth (write `NPM_TOKEN` into the npmrc pnpm actually
  reads) and keeping `changeset publish` — not covered here since the chosen direction is OIDC.

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

name: CI

# The PR gate: build, typecheck, test, lint, and the publish/provenance checks — everything `ready`
# plus the gates covers, split into parallel jobs. Runs on every PR and on pushes to main so a
# regression is caught before merge, not at docs-deploy or release-tag time.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Supersede in-flight PR runs; let main runs finish.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  # vp's task cache stores task OUTPUTS as .tar.zst tarballs, so a cache hit re-materializes the
  # gitignored generated dirs. The `build` job warms it; downstream jobs restore and replay
  # `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a cold rebuild.
  VP_TASK_CACHE: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
  VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX: vp-taskcache-

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore/save vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

  typecheck:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Typecheck
        run: vp check

  test:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Test all packages
        run: vp run -r test

  lint:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Lint CSS
        run: vp run lint:css
      - name: Lint JS
        run: vp run lint:js
      - name: Validate generated output
        run: vp run validate:generated:only
      - name: Lint Markdown
        run: vp run lint:markdown

  publint:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history so the changed-packages diff can reach the PR base / previous push.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Resolve changed packages
        id: changed
        env:
          CHANGED_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: node scripts/release/changed-packages.ts
      - name: Build and publint (scoped to changed packages)
        shell: bash
        env:
          SCOPE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.scope }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.packages }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "none" ]]; then
            echo "No publishable packages changed; skipping publint."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "all" ]]; then
            vp run -r build
            vp run gate:publint
            exit $?
          fi
          # publint only inspects the scoped packages, so build just their dependency closure ("...").
          build_filters=(); check_filters=()
          IFS=',' read -ra pkgs <<< "${PACKAGES}"
          for p in "${pkgs[@]}"; do
            [[ -n "${p}" ]] || continue
            build_filters+=("-F" "${p}...")
            check_filters+=("-F" "${p}")
          done
          echo "publint scoped to: ${pkgs[*]}"
          vp run "${build_filters[@]}" build
          vp exec "${check_filters[@]}" publint

  attw:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history so the changed-packages diff can reach the PR base / previous push.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Resolve changed packages
        id: changed
        env:
          CHANGED_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: node scripts/release/changed-packages.ts
      - name: Build and attw (scoped to changed packages)
        shell: bash
        env:
          SCOPE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.scope }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.packages }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "none" ]]; then
            echo "No publishable packages changed; skipping attw."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "all" ]]; then
            vp run -r build
            vp run gate:attw
            exit $?
          fi
          # attw only packs the scoped packages, so build just their dependency closure ("...").
          build_filters=(); check_filters=()
          IFS=',' read -ra pkgs <<< "${PACKAGES}"
          for p in "${pkgs[@]}"; do
            [[ -n "${p}" ]] || continue
            build_filters+=("-F" "${p}...")
            check_filters+=("-F" "${p}")
          done
          echo "attw scoped to: ${pkgs[*]}"
          vp run "${build_filters[@]}" build
          vp exec "${check_filters[@]}" attw --pack --profile strict --no-emoji --ignore-rules no-resolution cjs-resolves-to-esm

  repository:
    # Pure manifest read — no build needed. Catches a missing repository.url (which breaks npm OIDC
    # provenance) on the PR instead of at release.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Check repository metadata
        run: vp run gate:repository

  commitlint:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Lint PR commit messages
        run: vp exec commitlint --from "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}" --to "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" --verbose

  # Detect docs-relevant changes so PRs only pay for the docs build when the site could change. Runs on
  # both events (never skipped) so the `docs` job's `needs` is always satisfied.
  docs-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docs: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Detect docs-relevant changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            docs:
              - 'docs/**'
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'formats/**'
              - 'platforms/**'
              - 'renderers/**'
              - 'plugins/**'
              - 'design/**'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'

  # Build the site as part of CI, so:
  #  - PRs get the exact deploy command run — a broken build OR a stale translation cache
  #    (check-locale-drift) blocks the PR instead of only surfacing in the post-merge Deploy docs run.
  #  - main pushes upload the built site as `docs-site`, which the Deploy docs workflow publishes
  #    directly (no rebuild).
  # Gated on docs-relevant changes with the same path set the Deploy docs `changes` job uses, so the
  # artifact is uploaded exactly when a deploy will look for it.
  docs:
    needs: [build, docs-changes]
    if: needs.docs-changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Build docs (locale parity + drift + VitePress build)
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/
      # On main, hand the built site to the Deploy docs workflow (workflow_run) so it publishes without
      # rebuilding. The CNAME is baked in here so the downloaded artifact is deploy-ready as-is.
      - name: Add custom domain file
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME
      - name: Upload built docs site
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: docs-site
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist
          retention-days: 1
