name: Deploy docs

# Publish the VitePress + TypeDoc site to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.
#
# Gated behind CI: this runs after the CI workflow finishes on main and only deploys when CI passed.
# CI's `docs` job already builds the site on main and uploads it as `docs-site`, so this workflow just
# downloads that artifact and publishes it — no rebuild. `workflow_dispatch` is the manual escape hatch
# (a `[skip ci]` commit, or re-running a failed deploy): the CI artifact won't exist, so it builds fresh.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # download the build-output artifact from the triggering CI run
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Deploy only after a successful CI run (or a manual dispatch), and — for a CI-triggered run — only
  # when the pushed commit actually changed something the site renders.
  changes:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      should_deploy: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.should_deploy }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Decide whether to deploy
        id: decide
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            exit 0
          fi
          # The site is themed by generated token/CSS output from many packages, so treat those as
          # deploy-worthy too (broad but correct). Keep this path set in lockstep with CI's `docs-changes`
          # filter, so CI uploads the `docs-site` artifact exactly when this decides to deploy. Compare
          # the pushed commit to its parent.
          if git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | grep -qE '^(docs/|packages/|formats/|platforms/|renderers/|plugins/|design/|pnpm-lock\.yaml|pnpm-workspace\.yaml)'; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          else
            echo "should_deploy=false" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            echo "No docs-relevant changes in this push; skipping deploy."
          fi

  build:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.should_deploy == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      # Post-CI (the common path): CI already built the site on main and uploaded it as `docs-site`
      # (CNAME baked in). Just fetch it — no vp, no rebuild.
      - name: Download prebuilt docs site from CI
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: docs-site
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # Manual escape hatch (workflow_dispatch, e.g. a `[skip ci]` commit or re-running a failed
      # deploy): no CI artifact exists, so build the site fresh here.
      - name: Set up Vite+
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Build docs
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        run: vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build && vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/
      - name: Write custom domain file
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    and cuts a GitHub release per package.
#
# Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow GitHub Actions
# to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and an `NPM_TOKEN` secret.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so `changeset publish` ships real dist. Publish ignores lifecycle scripts (below), so a
      # package's `prepublishOnly` won't re-invoke a nested `vp` (which can fail with os error 22).
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"
          PNPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"

# Wire npm (OIDC) publishing into the changesets release flow

## Context

The automated release publishes via `changeset publish`, which detects the pnpm workspace and shells out
to `pnpm publish`. pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (returns 404, then silently skips OIDC — pnpm
issues [#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812), [#11513](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513);
same `E404` we hit). npm's OIDC ("trusted publishing") is the reference implementation and works, but only
through the **npm CLI**. The prior token path also broke (setup-vp mangles the `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`
placeholder in the npmrc → unauthenticated → `E404`).

Goal (per the user + the [yankeeinlondon/gha pattern](https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393)):
**token-free OIDC publishing**, while keeping changesets for versioning (the Version PR, per-package
CHANGELOGs) and getting git tags + GitHub releases. All 47 `@pantoken/*` packages already exist on npm,
so trusted publishing is viable (it attaches to existing packages).

Key enabler (confirmed in `changesets/action@v1` source): the action runs whatever `publish` command you
give it, parses its **stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
(`/New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)/`), and — with `createGithubReleases: true` — **creates the
git tags and GitHub releases itself** (release notes from each package's `CHANGELOG.md`). It does not
require `changeset publish`. So we let the npm CLI do `npm publish` and just print the `New tag:` lines.

## Plan

### 1. Publish with the npm CLI, driven by changesets — `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (new)
A publish script the changesets action calls (as its `publish` input) that uses `npm publish`, not pnpm:
- Enumerate publishable packages via `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()`
  (`scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`), in dependency order.
- Idempotency: skip any package whose current `version` is already on npm (`npm view <pkg>@<version>` —
  succeeds now that devEngines is `onFail: warn`); publish the rest.
- For each to-publish package: run `npm publish --provenance --access public` from the package dir. The
  npm CLI (≥ 11.5.1) performs the OIDC token exchange and emits provenance; no token.
- After each successful publish, print `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` to stdout. That's all the v1 action
  needs — it then pushes the git tag and creates the GitHub release per package (notes from its
  `CHANGELOG.md`). No tag/release logic in our script.
- Expose as the `release:publish` task in root `vite.config.ts` (replacing `vpx changeset publish`).

### 2. `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- Keep `changesets/action@v1` — it still runs `release:version` (Version PR) and now `release:publish`
  (our npm script), with `createGithubReleases: true` so it makes the tags + releases from the script's
  `New tag:` stdout. Drop the token: no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`.
- Before the action: `actions/setup-node` (node **≥ 22.14.0**, `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`)
  → `npm install -g npm@latest` (OIDC needs npm **≥ 11.5.1**; Node 22's bundled npm is too old) →
  `vp run -r build` (publish packs built `dist/`).
- Permissions: `id-token: write` (OIDC + provenance), `contents: write` (tags/releases),
  `pull-requests: write` (Version PR). Env: `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"`; drop the ignore-scripts vars
  (prepublishOnly already removed in #23).
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the action stays as-is for now (Version-PR-CI auto-run is the separate #20 concern).

### 3. Root `vite.config.ts`
- `release:publish` → `node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (was `vpx changeset publish`).
- `release:version` stays `vpx changeset version`.

## One-time prerequisite (manual — only the user can do this)
Configure a **trusted publisher on each package** at npmjs.com → package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
publisher = GitHub Actions, repo = `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow = `release.yml`. This release bumps
all 47 packages (4 core minor + 43 dependents via `updateInternalDependencies: patch`), so all 47 need it
before OIDC publish will succeed. There is no scope-wide setting; it's per package (check whether the npm
CLI/API can script it — otherwise the web UI, ~47 one-time). Until a package has its trusted publisher,
its `npm publish` 404s — the script logs and continues, so a partial config yields a partial release.

## Verification
- **Dry-run the publish logic locally** (no real publish): run `publish-npm.ts` with a `--dry-run` flag
  that lists which packages it *would* publish (version-not-on-npm check) and prints the tag/output lines,
  without calling `npm publish`. Confirm it selects `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0`
  + the bumped dependents and skips already-published ones.
- **Coverage/CI gates unaffected**: `scripts/` + `.github/` changes don't trip `release:coverage`; run it
  to confirm. Unit-test the pure parts of `publish-npm.ts` (package selection, output formatting) in
  `scripts/release/publish-npm.test.ts`, matching the existing release-script test pattern.
- **Real publish (after trusted publishers are configured)**: merge → watch the Release run → confirm
  npm shows `0.2.0` with a provenance badge, tags `@pantoken/x@0.2.0` exist, GitHub releases are created,
  and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` resolves. Re-running is idempotent
  (already-published versions are skipped).

## Notes / decisions
- **OIDC-only** (no token fallback): simplest, matches the move off tokens. The linked repo forks
  token-vs-OIDC; we can add that later if a token is ever reintroduced.
- **Provenance** comes for free with OIDC npm publish (it was already configured; unaffected).
- The 47-package trusted-publisher setup is the real cost of going token-free; flag it up front. If that's
  too heavy, the alternative is fixing the token auth (write `NPM_TOKEN` into the npmrc pnpm actually
  reads) and keeping `changeset publish` — not covered here since the chosen direction is OIDC.

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    and cuts a GitHub release per package.
#
# Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow GitHub Actions
# to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and an `NPM_TOKEN` secret.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so `changeset publish` ships real dist. Publish ignores lifecycle scripts (below), so a
      # package's `prepublishOnly` won't re-invoke a nested `vp` (which can fail with os error 22).
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"
          PNPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"

name: Deploy docs

# Publish the VitePress + TypeDoc site to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.
#
# Gated behind CI: this runs after the CI workflow finishes on main and only deploys when CI passed.
# CI's `docs` job already builds the site on main and uploads it as `docs-site`, so this workflow just
# downloads that artifact and publishes it — no rebuild. `workflow_dispatch` is the manual escape hatch
# (a `[skip ci]` commit, or re-running a failed deploy): the CI artifact won't exist, so it builds fresh.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # download the build-output artifact from the triggering CI run
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Deploy only after a successful CI run (or a manual dispatch), and — for a CI-triggered run — only
  # when the pushed commit actually changed something the site renders.
  changes:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      should_deploy: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.should_deploy }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Decide whether to deploy
        id: decide
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            exit 0
          fi
          # The site is themed by generated token/CSS output from many packages, so treat those as
          # deploy-worthy too (broad but correct). Keep this path set in lockstep with CI's `docs-changes`
          # filter, so CI uploads the `docs-site` artifact exactly when this decides to deploy. Compare
          # the pushed commit to its parent.
          if git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | grep -qE '^(docs/|packages/|formats/|platforms/|renderers/|plugins/|design/|pnpm-lock\.yaml|pnpm-workspace\.yaml)'; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          else
            echo "should_deploy=false" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            echo "No docs-relevant changes in this push; skipping deploy."
          fi

  build:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.should_deploy == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      # Post-CI (the common path): CI already built the site on main and uploaded it as `docs-site`
      # (CNAME baked in). Just fetch it — no vp, no rebuild.
      - name: Download prebuilt docs site from CI
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: docs-site
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # Manual escape hatch (workflow_dispatch, e.g. a `[skip ci]` commit or re-running a failed
      # deploy): no CI artifact exists, so build the site fresh here.
      - name: Set up Vite+
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Build docs
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        run: vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build && vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/
      - name: Write custom domain file
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

1	name: Release
2	
3	# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
4	#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
5	#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
6	#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
7	#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
8	#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
9	#
10	# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
11	# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
12	# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
13	# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
14	# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
15	# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.
16	
17	on:
18	  push:
19	    branches: [main]
20	  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)
21

23	  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
24	  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
25	  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)
26	
27	# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
28	concurrency:

30	  cancel-in-progress: false

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      # OIDC trusted publishing needs npm ≥ 11.5.1; Node 22's bundled npm is older. Upgrade the global npm
      # the publish script shells out to.
      - name: Upgrade npm for OIDC publishing
        run: npm install -g npm@latest

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

---
name: release-oidc-publish
description: How pantoken publishes to npm — npm-CLI OIDC (not pnpm/changeset publish), driven by the changesets action's stdout parsing
metadata:
  type: project
---

Releases are automated by `changesets/action@v1` in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Publishing does
**not** use `changeset publish` — that shells out to `pnpm publish`, and pnpm's OIDC token exchange is
broken (E404; pnpm #9812/#11513). Instead `release:publish` runs `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts`, which
uses the **npm CLI** (`npm publish --provenance --access public`) per package — npm ≥11.5.1 is the only
working OIDC "trusted publishing" client. Token-free: `id-token: write`, no `NPM_TOKEN`. The workflow does
`npm install -g npm@latest` because Node 22's bundled npm is too old.

Why this works with changesets: `changesets/action@v1` (v1.9.0) runs whatever `publish` command you give
it with `ignoreReturnCode: true`, parses its **stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
(`/New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)/`), and with `createGithubReleases: true` pushes each git tag
+ creates each GitHub release (notes from the package's CHANGELOG.md) *before* it looks at the exit code.
So publish-npm.ts prints one `New tag:` per success and exits non-zero if any failed — succeeded packages
still get released, failures still show red, re-runs are idempotent (skips versions already on npm via
`npm view`).

**Manual prerequisite (only the user can do):** each published package needs a trusted publisher on
npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher: GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow
`release.yml`). No scope-wide setting; ~per package. Until configured, that package's `npm publish` 404s.

As of 2026-07-23: `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0` + bumped dependents are still
UNPUBLISHED (all prior attempts failed on the pnpm-OIDC / token bugs). This OIDC path is the fix, pending
trusted-publisher setup + a release run. See [[cssdoc-system]] and the CDN work (0.2.0 is what makes the
CDN URLs resolve). Related: [[pantoken-architecture]].

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head ci/oidc-publish --title "ci: publish via npm oidc and bump github actions" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

Wire npm's OIDC "trusted publishing" into the changesets release flow, and bump the outdated GitHub Actions.

`changeset publish` shells out to `pnpm publish`, and pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (E404; pnpm #9812/#11513) — every publish 404'd. npm's OIDC is the working reference implementation, but only through the npm CLI. This replaces the publish step with an npm-CLI script the changesets action drives.

### Publish
- **`scripts/release/publish-npm.ts`** (new): enumerates publishable packages in dependency order, skips versions already on npm (`npm view`), runs `npm publish --provenance --access public` per package, and prints one `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` line per success. The `changesets/action@v1` parses that stdout (`ignoreReturnCode: true`) and — with `createGithubReleases: true` — pushes each git tag + creates each GitHub release *before* it inspects the exit code. So the script exits non-zero on partial failure: succeeded packages still get released, failures still show red, and re-runs are idempotent.
- **`release.yml`**: `npm install -g npm@latest` (OIDC needs ≥ 11.5.1), `createGithubReleases: true`, dropped `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN` and the ignore-scripts env. Token-free via `id-token: write` + per-package trusted publishers on npmjs.com.
- **`vite.config.ts`**: `release:publish` → the new script.

### Action version bumps (verified against live releases 2026-07-23)
- `actions/cache@v4` → `@v6` (+ `cache/restore`) — also clears the Node 20 deprecation warning.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v4` → `@v7`, `actions/download-artifact@v4` → `@v8`.
- Everything else was already current.

## Verification
- Unit tests: 6/6 (`scripts/release/publish-npm.test.ts`).
- Dry-run: plans `@pantoken/{utils,components,web-components,css}@0.2.0` + dependents (48 total), skips the 20 already on npm, `utils` before `components`.
- `release:coverage` passes (no shippable source changed → no changeset needed).
- Post-merge: watch the Release run for the npm provenance badge + created tags/releases, and confirm the `docs-site` artifact round-trips across the upgraded upload@v7/download@v8.

Supersedes #20 (the fine-grained PAT approach). Per-package trusted publishers are already configured.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

content.text: The publish went straight through (no pending changesets), the changesets action even logged **"No NPM_TOKEN found, but OIDC is available - using npm trusted publishing"** — yet every `npm publish` got `ENEEDAUTH`. name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      # OIDC trusted publishing needs npm ≥ 11.5.1; Node 22's bundled npm is older. Upgrade the global npm
      # the publish script shells out to.
      - name: Upgrade npm for OIDC publishing
        run: npm install -g npm@latest

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

content.text:
## What happened

The Release run on the #24 merge failed. It went **straight to publish** (no pending changesets on main, since the versions were already at 0.2.0), and every one of the 48 `npm publish` calls errored `ENEEDAUTH` — even though the changesets action correctly logged *"OIDC is available - using npm trusted publishing"*.

**Root cause:** [actions/setup-node#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551). `setup-node`'s `registry-url` always writes `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` into the npmrc. With the token unset (which OIDC requires), npm sees that empty auth entry, thinks auth is configured, and bails with `ENEEDAUTH` instead of falling back to the OIDC token exchange. OIDC was available — npm just never reached for it.

**Fix ([PR #25](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/25)):** strip the `_authToken` line from the npmrc after the toolchain is set up (`sed -i '/_authToken/d'`) — the confirmed workaround from that issue — and fold the npm upgrade + a `npm --version` echo into the same step.

## Next step — your call

Merging #25 triggers a fresh Release run that actually attempts the publish with working auth. Publishing 48 packages to npm is outward and hard to undo, so I'm leaving the merge to you rather than triggering it myself. When you merge:

- Watch [the Release workflow](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/actions/workflows/release.yml) — the `Prepare npm` step now prints the npm version (should be ≥ 11.5.1), and the publish should show provenance instead of `ENEEDAUTH`.
- It's idempotent: the 20 already-published versions skip, the 48 remaining retry. If any package's trusted publisher is missing, only that one fails (red step) while the rest still ship — re-run to retry.
- Then check that `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` resolves.

If a re-run is cleaner than a merge for you, the workflow also has `workflow_dispatch` — but note it runs the release.yml on `main`, so the fix has to land there first either way.

Sources: [actions/setup-node#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551), [npm trusted publishing docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/).

content.text:
You're right — that's real duplicated work. On any push to `main`, two workflows run in parallel and each builds every package:

- **CI** builds (the `build` job, replayed by the downstream jobs via the task cache).
- **Release** builds independently (`vp run -r build`) before the changesets action.

And the Release build is wasted in the *common* case: when you merge a feature PR, there are pending changesets, so the action only opens/updates the "Version Packages" PR — which needs no build at all. The build is only genuinely needed on the rarer publish path (when a Version PR merges and there are no changesets left).

The cleanest fix is to stop building in Release except when it's actually publishing: fold the build into the `release:publish` task (`dependsOn: ["build:all"]`) and drop the always-run build step. Then feature-merge pushes skip the build entirely, and Release stays self-contained (no coupling to CI). The alternative — making Release trigger *after* CI via `workflow_run` and reuse CI's cache (like `docs.yml` does) — removes the duplicate even on the publish path, but it delays every release until CI finishes and couples the two.

One caveat on timing: I'd keep this **out of #25**. #25 is the auth fix that has to produce a clean first publish; changing how/when the build runs on that same critical run adds risk. Better as a small follow-up once the publish is confirmed green.

content.thinking:
I'm checking the npm version and configuration details from this test run. The npm version is 12.0.1, which is well above the required 11.5.1, and the sed command ran silently on the npmrc file while npm install output the package changes. Despite these steps, I'm still seeing the authentication error for the npm registry, so the issue persists.

Now I'm reconsidering where npm might be reading its configuration from. The publish command runs through a spawned npm process in the package directory, and npm reads config from multiple layers — project-level .npmrc files, user config, global config, and environment variables. There could be a project-level .npmrc at the repo root or in a package subdirectory that's setting an `_authToken` and overriding my changes. Since the repo uses pnpm, there might also be a pnpm-generated .npmrc I need to check. I'm also wondering if the OIDC exchange requires reaching the registry without any auth header at all.

The real issue might be that the changesets action is detecting OIDC and printing that message, but then our separate npm publish subprocess isn't actually performing the OIDC exchange. For npm to do the exchange, it needs to check if there's already a configured auth token — if there is, it uses that instead of attempting OIDC. And for the exchange itself to work, npm needs the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` environment variables to be present.

These env vars should be inherited through the process chain (job → action step → vp → node → spawnSync), but I need to verify that the spawned npm subprocess is actually receiving them.

The changesets action uses getExecOutput which inherits the environment by default, so that should pass them through. But the error message is vague — I should look for more detailed npm output to see if npm even attempted OIDC authentication. Also, I'm second-guessing the trusted publisher config the user mentioned with "allowed actions: `npm publish`" — that doesn't sound like a standard npm trusted publisher field.

Let me focus on a more likely culprit: there's probably a `.npmrc` file in the repo that's interfering with the OIDC exchange. Either it's a committed file for pnpm configuration, or pnpm created one during setup. I need to check the repo for `.npmrc` files and get the full npm error output to understand what's actually happening.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about changesets action, npm OIDC trusted publishing, and ENEEDAUTH errors:

## Overview

npm trusted publishing with OpenID Connect (OIDC) is now generally available. Changesets works with npm's native OIDC when you use 'changeset publish'.

## ENEEDAUTH Error Troubleshooting

If you encounter an "Unable to authenticate" (ENEEDAUTH) error when publishing, first verify that the workflow filename matches exactly what you configured on npmjs.com, including the .yml extension. All fields are case-sensitive and must be exact.

Other important checks include:

- Ensure you're using GitHub-hosted runners, GitLab.com shared runners, or CircleCI cloud, as self-hosted runners are not currently supported.
- For GitHub Actions specifically, check that the id-token: write permission is set in your workflow.
- To publish from GitHub, your package's repository.url field in package.json must exactly match your GitHub repository.

## Changesets Action Architecture Issue

There's a known limitation with the changesets/action itself. To enable OIDC trusted publishing, you need to add id-token: write permission in that workflow and use npm publish with npm version >=11.5, but the action does both creating and publishing, when you only want to run the publish workflow when actually publishing to npm.

## Requirements

Trusted publishing requires npm CLI version 11.5.1 or later and Node version 22.14.0 or higher.

content.content:
# NPM OIDC Publishing Issues on GitHub Actions

## Root Cause

The primary issue wasn't with OIDC itself, but with a conflicting token. One user discovered that `actions/setup-node` sets a default `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable, which interfered with OIDC authentication.

## Resolution

**Clear the conflicting token** by explicitly setting it to an empty string:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: 24
    registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org/
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ""
```

## Concrete Requirements Mentioned

- **Node version**: Use version 24 or later for OIDC support
- **Registry URL**: Explicitly set `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org/`
- **Permissions**: Include `id-token: write` in workflow permissions
- **Trusted Publisher config**: Verify exact matches for organization name, repository URL, workflow filename, and environment name (watch for hidden spaces)
- **Package.json**: Include `repository.url` field matching your GitHub URL
- **npm version**: At least 11.5 recommended

The issue affected publishing from non-main branches because the token mismatch prevented proper OIDC token validation during npm publish attempts.

# GitHub Actions Workflow for npm Publishing with Changesets + OIDC

Here's the complete workflow YAML from the article:

```yaml
name: Publish Package
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write
  deployments: write
concurrency: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release & Publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: "pnpm"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Create Release PR or Publish
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          publish: pnpm release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

**Key findings:**

1. **setup-node config**: Sets `node-version: 24` (required for OIDC support), `registry-url`, and `cache: "pnpm"`. No `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable.

2. **npm upgrade**: The workflow doesn't explicitly upgrade npm; it relies on Node 24.

3. **Publishing method**: Uses `changesets/action@v1` with `publish: pnpm release` (which runs the script: `"pnpm run build && changeset publish"`).

4. **Permissions**: Includes `contents`, `pull-requests`, `id-token`, and `deployments` write permissions.

5. **.npmrc manipulation**: None present in this workflow.

# OIDC and NPM Authentication in Changesets Action

## OIDC Detection and Logging

The code logs this message when OIDC is available:

> "No NPM_TOKEN found, but OIDC is available - using npm trusted publishing"

When this condition is detected, **the script does nothing else**—it simply logs the message and continues without setting up any npm authentication files.

## NPM_TOKEN Authentication Setup

When `NPM_TOKEN` is present, the script:

1. Checks for an existing `.npmrc` file
2. Searches for an existing auth token entry matching the pattern `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=`
3. If no token exists, appends this line to `.npmrc`:

```
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${process.env.NPM_TOKEN}
```

If no `.npmrc` exists, it creates one with the auth token.

## Key Difference

The OIDC path skips all `.npmrc` file creation and modification. It relies on npm's native OIDC support (via `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` environment variables) to handle authentication without explicit token setup. The third fallback option assumes npm is already authenticated through other means.

Based on my search results, I found relevant information about the npm CLI's OIDC implementation. Here's what I found:

## Summary of npm CLI OIDC Conditions for Trusted Publisher Publishing

The npm CLI's oidc.js module is designed to handle OpenID Connect token retrieval and exchange for CI environments such as GitHub Actions and GitLab. It retrieves an OIDC token from the CI environment, exchanges it for an npm token, and sets the token in the provided configuration for authentication with the npm registry.

### Environment Variable Conditions

The environment variables `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` are automatically injected into GitHub Actions workflows, but only if the workflow declares `id-token: write` permissions.

The critical requirement is the id-token: write permission, which allows GitHub Actions to generate OIDC tokens.

### Supported CI Environments

The npm CLI detects when it's running in a supported CI environment, currently GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

### How npm Attempts OIDC Publishing

The npm publish command calls the OIDC utility with the package name, registry, options, and config parameters to attempt OIDC authentication.

### Provenance Configuration

The npm CLI adds "auto" or "default" provenance to publishes that use OIDC within GitHub and GitLab. It does this by checking the OIDC id token payload and checking if the repository's visibility is public or private—if it's public, it applies the equivalent of adding the `--provenance` flag.

The key takeaway is that npm's OIDC implementation requires the `id-token: write` permission in your GitHub Actions workflow, and the npm CLI will automatically detect the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` environment variables to facilitate the OIDC token exchange when attempting a publish.

Based on the code provided, here are the conditions that cause the `oidc` function to return early and skip OIDC token exchange:

1. **Not in a supported CI environment:**
   ```
   "if (!(ciInfo.GITHUB_ACTIONS || ciInfo.GITLAB || ciInfo.CIRCLE))"
   ```
   The function exits if running outside GitHub Actions, GitLab, or CircleCI.

2. **GitHub Actions without proper permissions:**
   ```
   "if (!(process.env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL &&
   process.env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN))"
   ```
   GitHub Actions workflows must have `id-token: write` permissions set.

3. **No ID token available:**
   ```
   "if (!idToken)"
   ```
   The function skips OIDC if the `NPM_ID_TOKEN` environment variable isn't set and GitHub Actions token retrieval fails.

4. **Failed GitHub token request:**
   If the fetch request to GitHub's ID token endpoint returns a non-OK status or lacks a `value` field in the response, the function returns early.

5. **Failed token exchange:**
   ```
   "if (!response?.token)"
   ```
   If the npm registry's token exchange endpoint doesn't return a token in the response body, OIDC is skipped.

In all these scenarios, npm proceeds with publishing without authentication via OIDC.

# OIDC publishing for initial package versions

Based on the GitHub issue, **publishing an initial version with OIDC is not currently supported**.

## Current limitation

The issue states that "it's not possible to publish the initial version of a package using OIDC, it needs to be published manually or using a token."

## Root cause

The npmjs.com interface requires a package to exist before you can access its settings to enable OIDC publishing. This creates a chicken-and-egg problem for new packages.

## Recommended workaround

While the issue doesn't explicitly state this as an official recommendation, the implied workaround is to publish the initial version using a traditional authentication token, then configure OIDC publishing for subsequent versions.

## Context

PyPI has already solved this by allowing OIDC configuration before a package exists. The npm team is considering a similar approach to close this gap. The issue was opened on September 1, 2025, but no maintainer responses or proposed solutions are included in the content provided.

# Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

# Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): verbose npm so the OIDC token-exchange HTTP shows inline.
          NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL: verbose

      # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): npm writes a full-detail debug log per invocation to ~/.npm/_logs. Those
      # logs record the OIDC token-exchange request/response — capture them so we can see exactly why the
      # exchange returns no token (ENEEDAUTH). Remove this once the OIDC publish is working.
      - name: Collect npm debug logs
        if: always()
        run: |
          mkdir -p npm-debug-logs
          cp -r ~/.npm/_logs/. npm-debug-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true
          ls -la npm-debug-logs || true
      - name: Upload npm debug logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: npm-debug-logs
          path: npm-debug-logs
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: warn

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): verbose npm so the OIDC token-exchange HTTP shows inline.
          NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL: verbose

      # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): npm writes a full-detail debug log per invocation to ~/.npm/_logs. Those
      # logs record the OIDC token-exchange request/response — capture them so we can see exactly why the
      # exchange returns no token (ENEEDAUTH). Remove this once the OIDC publish is working.
      - name: Collect npm debug logs
        if: always()
        run: |
          mkdir -p npm-debug-logs
          cp -r ~/.npm/_logs/. npm-debug-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true
          ls -la npm-debug-logs || true
      - name: Upload npm debug logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: npm-debug-logs
          path: npm-debug-logs
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: warn

run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          # Publish is invoked as plain `node`, NOT `vp run`: the `vp run` launcher scrubs the
          # `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN` env vars (and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`) from the task
          # subprocess, so npm logged "oidc Skipped because incorrect permissions for id-token" and fell
          # back to ENEEDAUTH. Running node directly under the action's env lets npm see the OIDC token
          # request vars and do the trusted-publishing exchange.
          publish: node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): verbose npm so the OIDC token-exchange HTTP shows inline.
          NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL: verbose

      # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): npm writes a full-detail debug log per invocation to ~/.npm/_logs. Those
      # logs record the OIDC token-exchange request/response — capture them so we can see exactly why the
      # exchange returns no token (ENEEDAUTH). Remove this once the OIDC publish is working.
      - name: Collect npm debug logs
        if: always()
        run: |
          mkdir -p npm-debug-logs
          cp -r ~/.npm/_logs/. npm-debug-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true
          ls -la npm-debug-logs || true
      - name: Upload npm debug logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: npm-debug-logs
          path: npm-debug-logs
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: warn

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout.
#
# Token-free: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`), not an
# `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow
# GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and a
# trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
# GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
# publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          # Publish is invoked as plain `node`, NOT `vp run`: the `vp run` launcher scrubs the
          # `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN` env vars (and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`) from the task
          # subprocess, so npm logged "oidc Skipped because incorrect permissions for id-token" and fell
          # back to ENEEDAUTH. Running node directly under the action's env lets npm see the OIDC token
          # request vars and do the trusted-publishing exchange.
          publish: node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): verbose npm so the OIDC token-exchange HTTP shows inline.
          NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL: verbose

      # TEMPORARY (diagnostic): npm writes a full-detail debug log per invocation to ~/.npm/_logs. Those
      # logs record the OIDC token-exchange request/response — capture them so we can see exactly why the
      # exchange returns no token (ENEEDAUTH). Remove this once the OIDC publish is working.
      - name: Collect npm debug logs
        if: always()
        run: |
          mkdir -p npm-debug-logs
          cp -r ~/.npm/_logs/. npm-debug-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true
          ls -la npm-debug-logs || true
      - name: Upload npm debug logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: npm-debug-logs
          path: npm-debug-logs
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: warn

Releases are automated by `changesets/action@v1` in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Publishing does
**not** use `changeset publish` — that shells out to `pnpm publish`, and pnpm's OIDC token exchange is
broken (E404; pnpm #9812/#11513). Instead the action's `publish:` runs `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts`,
which uses the **npm CLI** (`npm publish --provenance --access public`) per package — npm ≥11.5.1 is the
only working OIDC "trusted publishing" client. Token-free: `id-token: write`, no `NPM_TOKEN`. The workflow
does `npm install -g npm@latest` because Node 22's bundled npm is too old.

**Two hard-won gotchas (both fixed):**
1. **Invoke the publish script with plain `node`, NOT `vp run`.** The `vp run` launcher scrubs the
   `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN` env vars (and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`) from the task subprocess,
   so npm logged `oidc Skipped because incorrect permissions for id-token` and fell back to ENEEDAUTH.
   release.yml uses `publish: node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts`.
2. **The script owns git tags + GitHub releases** (`createGithubReleases: false`). The changesets action's
   `pushTag` does `git push origin <tag>` on a tag it assumes already exists locally (from `changeset
   publish`) and needs `persist-credentials` — neither held, so tags/releases failed while npm publish
   succeeded. publish-npm.ts instead runs `gh release create <tag> --target <sha>` (creates tag + release

content.text:
Done with the tags/releases work, and the CDN is genuinely resolving now. Here's where everything landed.

## Resolved

**0.2.0 is fully released.** css, components, utils, web-components @ 0.2.0 + dependents are on npm with provenance, and **all 67 tags + GitHub releases were backfilled** (releases went 10 → 77). The CDN serves the lean sheet: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.lean.css` → **HTTP 200, ~22.5 KB gzip**.

The whole failure chain, for the record:
1. `vp run` scrubbed the OIDC id-token env vars → npm skipped OIDC → ENEEDAUTH. **Fixed** by invoking the publish script with plain `node` (#27).
2. The changesets action's `pushTag` needed a local tag + persisted creds we don't provide → tags/releases failed. **Fixed** in [PR #28](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/28): the script now creates tag + release itself via `gh release create`, idempotently (dual-scheme aware, `--dry-run`/`--releases-only` modes). 7 tests pass; diagnostics from #26 removed.

Merge #28 and every future release self-heals: publish via OIDC, then ensure tag + release.

## One more thing I found — the CDN docs URLs are wrong

jsDelivr serves **raw file paths** and ignores a package's `exports` map. The files live under `dist/`, so:
- ✅ `…/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.lean.css` → 200
- ❌ `…/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` → 404 — and *that's* the form the picker and [docs/guide/cdn.md](docs/guide/cdn.md) advertise for every CSS/`combine` link (the web-components `.iife.js` example already includes `/dist/`).

So the advertised CDN links — the whole point of the original feature — currently 404. There's a fork on how to fix it:
- **Add `/dist/` to the advertised URLs** (picker + guide) — quick, but exposes the `dist/` path in public URLs.
- **Restructure the packages to ship the CSS at package root** — clean URLs as originally intended, but touches each package's build output, `files`, and `exports`.

Want me to take that on next, and if so, which direction? (I'd lean toward adding `/dist/` — it's a small, contained fix that makes the links work immediately, and we can prettify later.)

# CDN & distribution

pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.

## The token foundation

Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
variants ship:

- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.

The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
just the foundation loaded.

## Pick your components

jsDelivr's combine endpoint pulls the token foundation plus only the component stylesheets you need, in a
single request. Check the components you want, and the builder writes the URL:

<CdnPicker />

Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (about
0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
already carries them.

### Load order and fonts

Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` points at
font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
```

### Everything at once

Check **All components** in the picker to switch it to the barrel, or point at it yourself (about 141 KB
gzipped) alongside the token sheet:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
/>
```

## Web components

`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.

### ES modules (recommended)

An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
<script type="module">
  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
</script>
```

Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.

To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### A classic script tag

For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
```

It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
only when you can't use modules.

## Pinning versions

The URLs above — and the ones the picker writes — track the latest release. Pin a major (or exact)
version for production — for example `@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you.

## What's not here

There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.

# CDN & distribution

pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.

## The token foundation

Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
variants ship:

- `@pantoken/css/dist/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
- `@pantoken/css/dist/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.

The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
just the foundation loaded.

## Pick your components

jsDelivr's combine endpoint pulls the token foundation plus only the component stylesheets you need, in a
single request. Check the components you want, and the builder writes the URL:

<CdnPicker />

Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/dist/component-icons.css` (about
0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
already carries them.

### Load order and fonts

Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` points at
font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/dist/fonts.css" />
```

### Everything at once

Check **All components** in the picker to switch it to the barrel, or point at it yourself (about 141 KB
gzipped) alongside the token sheet:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/dist/components.css"
/>
```

## Web components

`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.

### ES modules (recommended)

An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.css" />
<script type="module">
  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
</script>
```

Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.

To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### A classic script tag

For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.css" />
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
```

It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
only when you can't use modules.

## Pinning versions

The URLs above — and the ones the picker writes — track the latest release. Pin a major (or exact)
version for production — for example `@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you.

## What's not here

There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.
